2- Vector Fan Grid: You activate industrial fans, turbine drones, pressure vents, traffic barriers, or directional force engines. Deal 3d10+10 techno damage and choose a direction the pressure is moving. Targets can’t move against that direction.

3- Chaffstorm Screen: You flood the zone with dust, chaff, smoke, scrap particles, sensor noise, and hostile visibility interference. Deal 5d6+9 techno damage. Attacks made from beyond Melee range have disadvantage.

Vital Beacon.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range.

On a success, spend a Hope to tag them with a vital scanner, surgical laser, bioelectrical flare, or diagnostic tracer, dealing d8+2 techno damage using your Proficiency.

The target becomes temporarily Vulnerable and remains visibly marked until this condition is cleared.

Field Patch.description: When you can take a few minutes to focus on a creature you’re helping, spend 2 Hope to use trauma foam, sutures, nanite gel, pain blockers, therapy software, or emergency stabilizers to clear a HP or a Stress. Once per long rest, when you spend this time learning something new about them or revealing something about yourself, you can clear 2 HP or 2 Stress on them instead.

Reassurance.description: Once per rest, after an ally attempts an action roll but before the consequences take place, you can offer guidance, calm their breathing, trigger a stabilizer, shout a practiced command, or talk them through shock. When you do, your ally can reroll their dice.

Emergency Procedure.description:
Make an Interface Roll (13) and target a creature other than yourself within Melee range.

On a success, mark a Stress to clear 2 HP or 2 Stress on the target. On a failure, mark a Stress to clear a HP or a Stress on the target.

You can’t heal the same target with Emergency Procedure again until your next long rest.

Last Record.description:
You can extract the final biological, neural, or cybernetic record from a corpse, damaged implant, memory chip, or dead biomonitor.

Make an Interface Roll (13).

On a success with Hope, you find the answer to three questions. On a success with Fear, you find the answer to one question.

The information is reliable, but you cannot discover anything beyond what the target knew or witnessed in life. On a failure, or after you find your answers, the body, implant, or data source becomes unusable for this protocol.

Second Wind.description:
Once per rest, when you succeed on an attack against an adversary, you can trigger adrenaline, endorphin spikes, pain blockers, combat drugs, or survival reflexes to clear 3 Stress or a HP.

On a success with Hope, you also trigger this for an ally within Close range that clears 3 Stress or a HP.

Lean On Me.description:
Once per long rest, when you stabilize, console, support, or talk an ally through a failed action roll, you can both clear 2 Stress.

This might look like grounding them through panic, forcing them to breathe, administering a calming dose, resetting their neural feedback, or simply refusing to let them spiral.

Death Lock.description:
Spend 3 Hope and choose an ally within Close range.

They are placed under a death-lock protocol, such as a cardiac override, neural backup, emergency blood pump, trauma stasis patch, or Last-chance Auto-injector.

When this ally would make a death move, they clear a Hit Point instead. This effect ends when it saves the target from a death move, you use Death Lock on another target, or you take a long rest.

Trauma Field.description:
Once per long rest, you can deploy a trauma field around you using medical drones, nanite mist, auto-injectors, or emergency triage beacons.

You and all allies within Close range clear a HP. Spend 2 Hope to allow you and all allies within Close range to clear 2 HP instead.

Emergency Fabricator.description:
Spend a Hope to deploy a compact medical fabricator, trauma printer, or emergency reconstruction tool.

You can create, reshape, reinforce, or repair a object or material within Close range, no larger than you.

This protocol is designed for medical, survival, and emergency use. For example, you can print a temporary prosthetic support, seal a wound, create a tool, stabilize damaged cyberware, or shape synthetic tissue. If you use this protocol to help a creature act through injury, or a failing system, they gain a +2 bonus to their next action roll.

This protocol can’t create weapons, complex machines, advanced electronics, ammunition, valuable goods, or permanent cyberware.

Shock Charge.description: Once per rest, spend 3 Hope to charge a weapon, implant, defibrillator rig, surgical tool, or neural overload strike. The next time you roll for damage, double the result of your damage roll.

Trauma Ward.description:
Make an Interface Roll (16). Once per long rest on a success, choose a point within Far range and deploy a trauma ward there for all allies within Very Close range of that point.

This might appear as a med-drone perimeter, hard-light clinic, surgical tent, nanite curtain, emergency stabilization field, or automated life-support zone. When you do, place a d6 on this card with the 1 value facing up. When an ally in this zone takes damage, they reduce it by the die’s value. You then increase the die’s value by one. When the die’s value would exceed 6, this effect ends.

Restoration Suite.description:
After a rest, place a number of tokens equal to your Interface trait on this card. Touch a creature and spend any number of tokens to clear 1 HP or 1 Stress for each token spent.

You can also spend 2 token from this card when touching a creature to clear a condition or treat a physical, cybernetic, or psychological ailment. The GM might require additional tokens depending on the severity of the ailment. After a rest, clear all tokens.

Combat Transfusion.description:
When you deal damage to a target, you can spend 2 Hope to clear a HP on an ally within Close range.

This might look like triggering a linked trauma patch, releasing stored nanites, or using the enemy’s exposed biology or machinery to power an emergency treatment.

Medtech-Synced.description:
When 4 or more of the domain cards in your loadout are from the Medtech Competency, gain the following:

Gain a +3 bonus to your Severe damage threshold.

Once per rest, when incoming damage would make you mark HP, you can mark that much Stress or spend that much Hope instead.

Impact Reducer.description: Mark a Stress to deploy a protective aura on a target within Close range, such as emergency plating, pain suppression, or nanite reinforcement. When the target marks an Armor Slot, they reduce the severity by an extra threshold. If this protocol causes a creature who would be damaged to instead mark no HP, the effect ends. You can only hold Impact Reducer on one creature at a time.

Rejuvenation Barrier.description:
Make an Interface Roll (15). Once per rest on a success, create a temporary barrier of mobile life-support shielding around you at Close range.

You and allies within the barrier when this protocol is activated clear 1d4 HP. While the barrier is active, you and allies within it have resistance to physical damage from outside the barrier. When you move, the barrier follows you.

Clinical Authority.description:
Make an Interface Roll (15) to activate a neurological presence enhancer. On a success, spend 2 Hope to make your Presence equal to your Interface trait until your next long rest.

While this protocol is active, a creature must mark a Stress when they target you with an attack.

Trauma Lance.description:
Make an Interface Roll (16).

On a success, mark any number of Stress to target a line of allies within Far range with surgical drones, trauma foam, life-support pulses, or emergency repair systems.

You can clear HP on the targets equal to the number of Stress marked, divided among them however you’d like.

Invigoration.description:
When you or an ally within Close range has used a feature that has an exhaustion limit, such as once per rest or once per session, you can spend any number of Hope and roll that many d6s. If any roll a 6, the feature can be used again.

This might represent emergency stimulants, memory backups, neural rebooting, adrenal flooding, cyberware overclocking, or forcing a body past its safe limits.

Lazarus Procedure.description:
Make an Interface Roll (20) over the body of a creature who died within the current scene.

The body must still be mostly recoverable, or there must be an intact brain, neural core, cybernetic backup, or vital implant you can work from. On a success, restore the creature to life using emergency surgery, synthetic organs, neural rebooting, clone tissue, or cybernetic replacement.

The restored creature clears all marked HP, then marks 3 Stress. They return alive, conscious, and stable, but physically and psychologically shaken. Until their next long rest, they are temporarily Vulnerable and can’t benefit from Lazarus Procedure again. Then roll a d6. On a result of 5 or lower, place this card in your vault permanently.

Bare Metal.description: When you choose not to equip armor, your reinforced body, subdermal plating, hardened bones, or defensive cyberware gives you a base Armor Score of 3 + your Strength and the following base damage thresholds: Tier 1: 9/19 Tier 2: 11/24 Tier 3: 13/31 Tier 4: 15/38

Kinetic Push.description:
Make an attack with your weapon against a target within Melee range. On a success, you deal damage and knock them back to Close range. On a success with Hope, add a d6 to your damage roll.

Additionally, you can spend a Hope to make them temporarily Vulnerable.

Interpose.description: When an ally within Very Close range would take damage, you can mark a Stress to throw yourself into the line of fire, raise a defense, trigger your armor rig, or physically block the attack. You become the target of the attack instead. When you take damage from this attack, you can mark any number of Armor Slots.

Impact Frame.description:
You use the full force of your body, armor, shield, exo-frame, or reinforced limbs in a fight.

On a successful attack using a weapon with a Melee range, gain a bonus to your damage roll equal to your Strength.

Commanding Bulk.description:
When you make a Presence Roll, you can spend a Hope to add your Strength to the roll.

Additionally, once per rest when you would gain a condition, you can describe how your armored presence, combat discipline, sheer mass, or defensive posture helps you endure it and avoid gaining the condition.

Tactical Rally.description:
Once per rest, when you critically succeed on an attack, all allies within Very Close range can clear a Stress or gain a Hope.

This might look like a shouted command, a decisive opening, or a moment where your allies see that the line is still holding.

Lockdown Hold.description:
When you position yourself behind a creature who’s about your size, you can mark a Stress to pull them into a lockdown hold using a chokehold, joint lock, or restraint cable. The target becomes temporarily Vulnerable.

When a creature attacks a target who is Vulnerable in this way, they deal an extra 2d6 damage.

Support Tank.description:
When an ally within Close range fails a roll, you can spend 2 Hope to allow them to reroll either their Hope Die or Fear Die.

This might look like providing cover, forcing the enemy’s attention onto you, or bracing them through impact.

Repulsion Pulse.description: Make an Interface Roll against all targets within Melee range. Targets you succeed against are forced back to Far range and take d8+3 impact or techno damage using your Interface trait. This might look like a shield discharge, repulsor plate, pressure wave, or defensive blast from your armor rig.

Armor Tech.description:
While you’re wearing armor, gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Score.

During a rest, when you choose to repair your armor as a downtime move, your allies also clear an Armor Slot.

Rally Strike.description:
Once per rest, when you critically succeed on an attack, you and all allies who can see or hear you can clear a Hit Point or 1d4 Stress.

This might look like a shouted command, a decisive opening, or a moment where your allies see that the line is still holding.

Inevitable.description:
When you fail an action roll, your next action roll has advantage.

Your armor recalibrates, your stance hardens, or your threat model updates.

Rise Up.description: Gain a bonus to your Severe damage threshold equal to your Proficiency. When you mark 1 or more Hit Points from an attack, clear a Stress.

Shrug It Off.description:
When you would take damage, you can mark a Stress to reduce the severity of the damage by one threshold.

When you do, roll a d6. On a result of 3 or lower, place this card in your vault.

Aegis-Synced.description:
When 4 or more of the domain cards in your loadout are from the Aegis Competency, gain the following:

Gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Score.

When you mark 1 or more Hit Points without marking an Armor Slot, clear an Armor Slot.

Full System Surge.description: Once per long rest, mark 3 Stress to push your body, armor, cyberware, combat drugs, reinforcement frame, and defensive systems to their limits. Gain a +2 bonus to all of your character traits until your next rest.

Shockwave Slam.description:
Spend 2 Hope to strike the ground where you stand using a kinetic hammer, gravity boot, hydraulic fist, shield piston, exo-frame impact system, or reinforced body slam.

Make a Strength Roll against all targets within Very Close range. Targets you succeed against are thrown back to Far range and must make a Reaction Roll (17).

Targets who fail take 4d10+8 impact damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.

Hold the Line.description:
Describe the defensive stance you take and spend a Hope. If an adversary moves within Very Close range, they’re pulled into Melee range and Restrained.

This condition lasts until you move, fail a roll with Fear, or the GM spends 2 Fear on their turn to clear it.

Lead by Example.description:
When you deal damage to an adversary, you can mark a Stress and describe how you encourage your allies, draw fire, expose a weakness, or prove the enemy can be broken.

The next PC to make an attack against that adversary can clear a Stress or gain a Hope.

Unbreakable.description:
When you mark your last Hit Point, instead of making a death move, you can roll a d6 and clear a number of Hit Points equal to the result.

Then place this card in your vault.

Unyielding Armor.description:
When you would mark an Armor Slot, roll a number of d6s equal to your Proficiency.

If any roll a 6, reduce the severity by one threshold without marking an Armor Slot.

Neurospike.description: Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, mark a Stress to fire a hostile neurospike, overload pulse, rageware signal, pain-editor exploit, or illegal combat firmware into the target, dealing d10 techno damage using your Proficiency. On a success with Hope, the target also marks a Stress. On a roll with Fear, you must also mark a Stress.

Last-Resort Chip.description:
Mark a Hit Point to create a last-resort chip, emergency override patch, adrenaline key, survival trigger, or illegal biofeedback token powered by your own unstable systems.

Whoever carries it gains the following benefit:

Whenever the bearer would mark 2 or more HP, they can spend a Hope to reduce the HP marked by 1.

The chip burns out if you have no HP marked or you use this protocol again.

Pain Conversion.description:
If you have at least one HP marked, you gain a bonus to your damage rolls equal to twice your number of marked HP.

Your pain editor, adrenal engine, threat processor, or aggression software converts physical damage into combat output.

Aggression Feedback.description:
When you deal damage to a creature, mark a Stress to lock their threat profile into your Redline system. Until this feedback ends, your combat implants, adrenal processors, pain editor, and aggression software remain fixated on the target. You always know the direction of it relative to you. Additionally, each time that creature deals damage to you or an ally within Very Close range of you, your Redline system fires a hostile feedback spike back through the link, forcing them to mark a Stress.

This feedback ends when you use this protocol again.

Neurochemical Override.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Very Close range. If you use this protocol on an ally, roll with advantage. On a success, mark a Stress and choose one of the following effects:

1- The target grows calmer, stabilized by sedatives or neural regulation, and clears a Stress. On a success with Hope, they clear 2 Stress.

2- The target grows more anxious, overloaded by adrenaline, panic chemicals, or hostile feedback, and marks a Stress. On a success with Hope, they mark 2 Stress.

Redline Detonation.description:
Make an Interface Roll (12). On a success, mark a HP as you force your Redline systems past safe limits, dumping excess heat, neural overload, aggression feedback, or unstable cyberware output into a point within Far range.

A violent pulse of thermal distortion, pressure shock, sensor scream, or overclock fallout fills the area within Very Close range of that point.

Each target within the area marks 1 HP. On a success with Hope, each target within the area marks 2 HP instead.

System Hijack.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a creature within Far range. On a success, spend a Hope to hijack the target’s muscles, cyberware, nervous system, pain response, or nervous system for a brief violent burst. You can cause the target to move, attack, or both. If you do both, you choose the order.

If you cause the creature to move, they move to a location you choose within Close range of them.

If you cause the creature to attack, make an Interface Roll against a target within Melee range of them.

On a success, deal d10 physical damage using your Proficiency.

Killhook.description:
You launch a killhook, magnetic spike, tendon cable, monowire harpoon, recoil anchor, or combat grapnel at a location or creature within Far range. If the target is a location, make an Interface Roll (13). On a success, mark a Stress to pull yourself to a position within Melee range of it.

If the target is a creature, make an Interface Roll against it. On a success, mark a Stress to deal 3d8 physical damage to the target. You then pull the target straight toward yourself or pull yourself straight toward the target, ending within Melee range of it.

Emergency Stim Share.description:
Once per rest, mark a HP to flood each ally within Close range with combat drugs, trauma stabilizers, emergency stimulants, or pain suppressors.

Each affected ally clears a HP or a Stress. You can mark a Stress to allow those allies to clear one of each instead.

Feedback Retaliation.description:
When an attack from a creature causes you to mark one or more HP, you can make a Reaction Roll using your Interface trait against the creature. On a success, your Redline system converts the impact into a hostile backlash through your combat firmware, shock relays, rageware, or neural feedback implants, forcing the creature to mark the same number of HP as you did.

You can’t use this protocol again until you finish a rest.

Cortical Splinter.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a creature within Very Far range.

On a success, mark a HP to deploy a cortical splinter, neural spyware, biochip packet, or pain-loop signal that burrows into the target’s system. On a success with Hope, the target isn’t aware of the splinter.

You have advantage on Presence Rolls against the target, and whenever they make a roll, you can spend a Hope to give the roll disadvantage.

You can destroy the splinter to cause the target to mark a HP.

Redline Ward.description:
Mark a HP to deploy a Redline Ward around yourself at Very Close range. This might look like a haze of coolant vapor, warning lights, pressure distortion, combat drug mist, hostile sensor static, or unstable cyberware output bleeding into the air around you While in the ward, you have resistance to your choice of physical or techno damage. Choose when you activate this protocol. Allies also gain this benefit while in the ward.

The ward disappears if you move out of it, mark 2 or more HP, or use this protocol again.

Redline Ward (physical).description: Resistance to physical damage inside the ward.

Redline Ward (techno).description: Resistance to techno damage inside the ward.

Neuromuscular Lock.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, mark a Stress as you attack the target’s muscles, cyberware, nerves, blood pressure, or motor control.

The target becomes temporarily Restrained and temporarily Vulnerable. Each time the target is spotlighted while either of these conditions persists on them, they take d10 techno damage using your Proficiency.

This protocol ends early on the target if you use it again.

Redline-Synced.description:
When 4 or more of the domain cards in your loadout are from the Redline Competency, gain the following:

When you take enough damage to mark 2 or more Hit Points, gain a Hope.

For every 3 Hit Points you have marked, gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion.

Siphon Strike.description:
When you make a successful attack roll against an adversary and cause them to mark 2 or more HP, you can spend a Hope to clear a HP or Stress.

This might look like your adrenal system spiking, your pain editor stabilizing, your combat firmware rewarding violence, your body briefly mistaking impact for recovery, or forcing your body to stabilize through adrenaline.

Shared Overload.description:
Spend a Hope to allow you and a willing ally within Far range to redistribute marked HP between the two of you. This might look like linked trauma pumps, shared pain editors, emergency blood exchange, synchronized life-support, mirrored cyberware stress, or a dangerous neural bridge that spreads the damage across two unstable systems.

You can’t target that ally again with Shared Overload until you finish a rest.

Adrenaline Stack.description:
Your Redline systems have seeped into your bloodstream, enhancing your body in moments of urgency.

When you roll with advantage, use a d8 instead of a d6 as your advantage die if you have 1 or more HP marked.

After you make a Strength, Agility, or Finesse Roll, you can mark a HP to roll 1d8 and add it to the result.

Psycho Surge.description:
Once per rest, spend a Hope to unleash a violent surge of adrenaline, neural noise, rageware instability, overheating implants, pain-editor failure, and cyberpsychosis-adjacent aggression around yourself.

Make a single Interface Roll against each adversary within Close range. On a success, a target marks a HP and a Stress. On a failure, a target marks a Stress.

Each ally within Close range marks a Stress but clears a HP.

System Rupture.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a creature within Far range. On a success, mark a HP to mark the target with a trauma amplifier, wound exploit, neural instability feedback, pressure spike, or hostile nanite brand.

This mark lasts until the GM spends 2 Fear to remove it or you take Severe damage.

Whenever the target marks any HP while the mark remains, you can mark a Stress to make them mark an additional HP.
Whenever it marks HP, whoever applied this can mark 1 Stress to make it mark 1 additional HP. Lasts until the GM spends 2 Fear or whoever applied it takes Severe damage.

Refuse Shutdown.description: When you would mark your last HP, spend a Hope to mark a Stress instead. Your backup heart, emergency stim, pain editor, adrenal flood, or survival implant refuses to let your body shut down.

Kill-Switch Overdrive.description:
Make an Interface Roll against an adversary within Close range. On a success, spend 2 Hope to mark 1-3 HP. The target marks twice the number of Hit Points you marked. If this causes the target to mark their last HP, you can clear the HP you marked to activate this protocol.

This might look like a lethal overclock strike, rageware execution, neural kill-switch, cyberware burnout, adrenal detonation, or a point-blank system crash that converts the target’s collapse into your survival.

Corruption Spike.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, the target takes d6 techno damage using your Proficiency as a corrupted signal, Black ICE packet, or hostile daemon tears through their system.

The next time the target deals damage, that damage is reduced by 1d6.

On a success with Fear, the target instead takes d10 techno damage using your Proficiency.

Corrupted.description: The next damage this target deals is reduced by 1d6.

Dead Channel.description: You let a corrupted AI speak through a dead channel, broken speaker, or hijacked implant to torment a target. Make an Interface Roll against a creature you can see. On a success, they must mark a Stress and become temporarily Vulnerable.

Blackwall Shroud.description:
Make an Interface Roll (10). On a success, spend any number of Hope and place an equal number of tokens on this card to wrap yourself in sensor noise, digital shadow, corrupted overlays, haunted AI, or signal distortion.

After an attack roll is made against you, you can spend any number of tokens to gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion per token against that attack.

Backlash Daemon.description: When an ally within Close range takes damage from a target you can see, you can make a Reaction Roll against that target using your Interface trait. On a success, mark a Stress to unleash a retaliatory daemon, system scream, or invasive Black ICE backlash, dealing d6 techno damage using your Proficiency.

Drain Signal.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, once per short rest, the target takes d8 techno damage using your Proficiency and you clear 2 HP. On a success with Fear, you clear 3 HP instead.

This might look like draining power, stealing biofeedback, siphoning processor load, feeding on neural panic, or letting a daemon extract something useful from the target.

Panic Script.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, the target marks 1d4 Stress as you flood their HUD, senses, implants, or systems with corrupted signals.

You can choose to make the target run one range away from you. You can also spend a Hope to make the target temporarily Vulnerable.

Neural Burden Sync.description:
Once per rest, you can redistribute any marked HP between two willing targets you can touch.

This might look like synchronizing forbidden Blackwall data, redistributing system strain, offloading neurological collapse, or splitting pain across linked biomonitors between two bodies.

System Decay.description: Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, spend a Hope to infect them with corrupted firmware or obsolete code that their system no longer know how to process. The target becomes temporarily Degraded. While Degraded, the target uses a d12 instead of a d20 for attack rolls. You can only hold this protocol on one creature at a time.

Daemon Proxy.description: Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, spend a Hope to call forth a daemon proxy, hostile construct, AI splinter, or digital horror to attack the target and deal d10 techno damage using your Proficiency. The target must also make a Reaction Roll (12) to steel themselves against the intrusion. On a failure, they mark 1d4 Stress. After making the attack, the proxy dissipates.

Ghost Fog.description:
Make an Interface Roll (13). On a success, spend a Hope to flood the area around you with ghost fog: sensor static, chaff mist, corrupted light, digital afterimages, or invasive route-mapping projections.

You and any targets within Close range become momentarily incorporeal to security systems and automated barriers, allowing you to pass through a sealed passage that has a plausible physical or digital bypass.

This protocol lasts until you have passed through the barrier successfully.
Incorporeal to security systems and automated barriers until passing through the barrier.

Relic Edge.description:
Spend a Hope to load your weapon with a Blackwall combat routine until your next rest.

When you make an attack with this weapon, use your Interface trait instead of the trait it normally calls for. On a success, roll a number of d8s equal to the current number of Fear the GM has, up to your level, and deal that much techno damage as the target’s cyberware, nervous system, or armor interface is cut open by corrupted code.

If you succeed with Fear, the target must also mark a Stress.
Attacks with the loaded weapon use Interface and deal d8 techno damage per GM Fear (up to your level).

Corrupted Protocol.description:
Make an Interface Roll against all adversaries within Close range. You can spend a Hope for any target you succeeded against, forcing them to make a Reaction Roll (14).

On a failure, they take 8d6+6 techno damage as they are corrupted protocol of a self-destructive AI. On a success, they take half damage.

Tracewalk.description: Whenever you deal techno damage to a target, you can mark a Stress to immediately follow the trace and move into Melee range with that creature. This movement ignores difficult terrain and environmental interference, but it must follow a plausible physical, digital, or tactical route through the scene.

Blackwall-Synced.description:
When 4 or more of the domain cards in your loadout are from the Blackwall Competency, gain the following:

When you succeed with Fear, you can mark 2 Stress to prevent the GM from gaining a Fear.

Once per short rest, when making an action roll, you can add a +1 to the roll for each Fear the GM have.

Blackwall Manifestation.description: Make an Interface Roll (13). On a success, you force a fragment of the Blackwall to manifest between two points within Far range as a corrupted digital wall spilling into physical space. It does not appear as a solid wall, but as a violent fracture of static, hostile code, and AI corruption expressed through the surrounding environment. This lasts until you mark your next HP. Any creature inside the wall when it appears, or that passes through it, marks 2 Stress, then must succeed a Reaction Roll (16) or are Restrained.

Daemon Army.description:
Make an Interface Roll (14). Once per rest on a success, mark a Stress to release eight daemon AI fragments within Close range that move with you. Place a d8 on this card set to 8, representing the size of your daemon army. Whenever you deal damage to a target within Close range, you can decrease this value by 1 to deal an additional 1d8 techno damage.

When you take damage, you can decrease this value by 1 to reduce the damage by 1d8.

Each time the die is decreased, a daemon acts on your behalf, then disappears. When the die’s value would be reduced below 1, return this card to your vault.

Corrupted Shell.description:
You allow the Blackwall to partially rewrite your body, armor, implants, and nervous system.

While this card is active in your loadout:

For every 2 Stress you have marked, increase your thresholds by +1.

Whenever you succeed with Fear on an action roll, you can spend a Hope to clear an Armor Slot.

Total System Crash.description:
Make an Interface Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, mark 3 Stress and roll a number of d20s equal to your Interface trait, dealing that much techno damage to them.

If this damage is enough to defeat, disable, or destroy the target, all adversaries within Far range of the target must mark a Stress.

This might look like a catastrophic cyberware crash, mass hallucination, corrupted command cascade, terminal Black ICE burn, or rogue AI execution routine.

Feed on Panic.description:
Whenever a creature within Close range marks any number of Stress or takes Severe damage, you can spend a Hope to clear a Stress or clear a Fear the GM holds.

This might look like your system harvesting panic data, converting suffering into processing power, or letting something beyond the wall feed through your interface.

Invoke Shutdown.description:
When you deal damage to a creature that has all of its Stress marked, double the damage.

If this defeats, disables, or destroys them, you clear a Stress. If it doesn’t defeat, disable, or destroy them, they are permanently Vulnerable.

This might look like a kill command, identity collapse, full nervous-system lock, or a shutdown signal that leaves the target forever compromised.

Blackwall Host.description:
You can mark a Stress to become an Blackwall Host, allowing a rogue AI, corrupted daemon, lost military system, or forbidden Blackwall fragment to partially pilot your body. While in this form, gain the following: All adversaries within Close range must spend an additional Fear when using a Fear feature.

When you defeat, disable, or destroy a creature within Close range, you absorb their final output and clear a Hit Point.

You can mark a Stress to move to any location within Very Far range, ignoring difficult terrain, automated security, and environmental obstacles. This movement can’t pass through sealed barriers or spaces with no plausible route.

Every time you make an action roll in this form, you must spend a Hope. If you can’t, the breach collapses and you drop this form.
Adversaries within Close range spend 1 additional Fear on Fear features. Before each action roll, spend a Hope or leave the form.

Runner.description:
Network, hacking, Access, digital warfare
"Every locked system is just a door waiting to be taught fear."

Play a Runner if you want to… Break into networks, hijack drones, unlock systems, expose weakpoints, and turn hacking into battlefield control.

Class Items: An illegal cyberdeck with a custom interface or a stolen access shard from a job that should have killed you.

Hacking and Breaches: When you succeed on an Interface Roll to hack a connected system, you create a Breach. A Breach is a temporary opening in a system. When you create a Breach, spend it immediately to choose one Hack: Open/Lock, Loop/Spoof, Pull Data, Jam, Expose, or Command.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: Who taught you how to run systems, and what did they warn you never to touch?
What was the first network you broke into, and what did you find there?
Which corporation, gang, or government system still has your trace buried somewhere inside it?
connections: I once erased evidence that could have ruined you. What did I delete?
You saw me jack into a system that nearly killed me. What did you do to pull me out?
I know a secret about you because of something I found in a network. Do you know that I know?

Infiltrator.description:
Ghost, stealth, assassination, sabotage
"The best entry is the one no one remembers."

Play an Infiltrator if you want to… Move unseen, bypass security, disappear from danger, sabotage operations, and leave no trace behind.

Other mercenaries can hide, sneak, or bypass security. Infiltrators turn those moments into a profession. They feel the exact second when a target becomes vulnerable.

Class Items: A set of false credentials or a suppressed weapon from a job that officially never happened.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: What was the first place you broke into that should have been impossible?
Did you become an Infiltrator through training, coercion, desperation, or betrayal?
What target did you fail to eliminate, and what did it cost you?
connections: Which character knows one of your false identities?
Who do you trust to cover your exit?
What secret did you learn about another character but choose not to use?

Solo.description:
Assault, weapons, violence, combat dominance
"When the shooting starts, I become the plan."

Play a Solo if you want to… Win fights through weapon mastery, tactical aggression, suppressive fire, heavy offense, and relentless pressure.

Solos are professional combatants, hired guns, assault specialists, and battlefield killers who survive by ending threats before they become problems. They are the mercenaries called when the job turns loud.

Class Items: A customized weapon with a name or a damaged dog tag from the fight that made your reputation.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: What weapon do you trust more than most people?
What battle, contract, or massacre made your name known?
What kind of fight still scares you?
connections: Who pulled you back from going too far?
Who do you trust to stand beside you when the job turns loud?
Which character once saved you after a fight you should not have survived?

Augmented.description:
Chrome, cyberware, movement, body optimization
"Flesh was the prototype."

Play an Augmented if you want to… Push your body beyond natural limits through reinforced limbs, mobility implants, enhanced senses, and chrome-built precision.

Augmented are mercenaries who turned their own bodies into their livelihood. They know how to move with metal bones, strike with calibrated limbs, survive with artificial organs, and push their systems without immediately burning out.

Class Items: A maintenance kit for your most important implant or the original piece of your body that was replaced by chrome.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: What was your first implant, and why did you get it?
Which part of your original body do you miss most?
Did you choose to become an Augmented, or was your body rebuilt after something terrible?
connections: Which character knew you before the chrome?
Who helped you survive a bad installation?
Who treats your body like a person, not a machine?

Tech.description:
Systems, engineering, drones, equipment
"Give me parts, tools, and ten minutes."

Play a Tech if you want to… Build tools, repair systems, deploy devices, control drones, modify equipment, and turn preparation into power.

Techs are problem solvers who understand that every machine has a way to break, bend, or become useful. They make impossible plans work just long enough to matter.

Class Items: A customized toolkit full of illegal adapters and scavenged parts, or a broken machine you refuse to stop repairing.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: What machine, weapon, drone, or device do you refuse to abandon?
What piece of technology failed you when you needed it most?
Did you become a Tech because you loved machines, or because people were less reliable?
connections: Who broke something important that you still have not forgiven?
Who trusts your machines more than they trust you?
Which character helped you carry, hide, or rebuild something illegal?

Broker.description:
Influence, contacts, manipulation, reputation
"Everyone has a price. The trick is learning what currency they accept."

Play a Broker if you want to… Negotiate contracts, manipulate factions, command social pressure, build networks of favors, weaponize reputation, and win before the guns come out.

Brokers are negotiators, public faces, and social predators who understand that power rarely sits in the hands of the person holding the gun. They know who pays, who can be bought, and who needs to disappear before the next contract begins.

Class Items: A contact list worth more than your bank balance or a contract chip containing a big and illegal corporate deal.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: Who gave you your first real contact?
Which faction owes you, and which faction wants you dead?
What secret are you keeping because it is more valuable unsold?
connections: Which character did you recruit, rescue, hire, or buy out of trouble?
Who knows when you are lying?
Who has a debt to you that neither of you talks about?

Reclaimer.description:
Frontier, survival, ruins, hostile zones
"The old world is dead. That does not mean it is empty."

Play a Reclaimer if you want to… Survive beyond corporate control, cross dead zones, read terrain, salvage lost tech, navigate ruins, exploit hostile environments, and turn the battlefield itself into a tool.

Reclaimers are survivors who know how to live where civilization failed. They cross dead cities and see routes, shelter, and resources of the old world waiting to be used.

Class Items: A cracked route-map filled with personal markings or a piece of salvage from the place that should have killed you.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: What did you recover from the ruins that changed your life?
Were you raised outside the cities, on the road, or in a place the corps abandoned?
What vehicle, route, or piece of salvage do you refuse to abandon?
connections: Which character did you guide through a place that should have killed them?
Who trusts your routes more than they trust the map?
Which character has seen you risk everything for a vehicle, road, or piece of old tech?

Trauma Doc.description:
Medtech, medicine, surgery, survival
"Death is just a system failure with a narrow repair window."

Play a Trauma Doc if you want to… Keep the crew alive, perform battlefield surgery, stabilize cyberware, use medical drones, revive allies, and turn injury into a problem you can solve.

Trauma Docs are field medics, black-clinic surgeons, and cyberware miracle workers who know how to keep people alive when the world has already decided they should be dead.

Class Items: A trauma kit full of illegal pharmaceuticals and tools, or a bloodstained patient tag from someone you could not save.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: Who was the first person you failed to save?
What procedure did you perform that should have been impossible?
What illegal drug, implant, or technique do you know far too well?
connections: Who refuses to follow your medical instructions?
Which character knows what you do when there are not enough supplies for everyone?
Which character did you patch up after a job they still will not talk about?

Warden.description:
Aegis, protection, armor, interception
"If they want the crew, they go through me."

Play a Warden if you want to… Protect allies, absorb damage, control space, wear heavy armor, intercept attacks, survive impossible pressure, and become the hardest thing on the battlefield to move.

Wardens are bodyguards, riot breakers, and professional protectors who survive by making themselves the hardest problem in the room while they stand between the crew and whatever wants them dead.

Class Items: A defensive rig marked by old impacts or a contract token from someone you swore to protect.

Note: suggested traits and equipment vary by subclass — see the "Suggested Build" note on your chosen subclass.
backgroundQuestions: Who taught you to put yourself between danger and someone else?
Who did you fail to protect?
What part of your armor, shield, or defensive rig has saved your life the most?
connections: Which character have you personally carried out of danger?
Which character once protected you when you could not protect yourself?
Who knows the name of someone you failed to save?

Hold Your Breach.description: After you create a Breach, spend a Hope to use it without spending it.

Exploit.description: Mark a Stress to temporarily Exploit a target within Far range. While Exploited, the target gains a penalty to their Thresholds and Difficulty equal to your Tier. The maximum number of creatures you can Exploit at one time is equal to your Interface trait.

Exploited.description: Penalty to Thresholds and Difficulty equal to the Tier of the Runner who Exploited this target.

Clean Exit.description:
Spend 3 Hope when you would be discovered, trigger an alarm, or be targeted by an attack. You immediately become Hidden and move to a point within Close range.

  • If this was triggered by an attack, the attack has disadvantage.
  • If this was triggered by discovery or an alarm, it is delayed until your next Spotlight.

Cover Work.description:
You have a resource called Cover. When you roll with Hope while using a Ghost card, using stealth, disguise, misdirection, or a prepared route, gain 1 Cover. You can hold up to 3 Cover.

Spend 1 Cover to do one of the following:

  • Setup: Gain a +2 bonus to a roll made to hide, infiltrate, sabotage, impersonate someone, or bypass security.
  • Takedown: Add 1d6 to the damage roll when you deal damage to a target you are Hidden from, that is unaware of you, or that is Vulnerable.

You lose all unspent Cover when the scene ends.

On the sheet: this feature's counter shows your Cover. Use "Gain Cover" after a fitting roll with Hope; Setup and Takedown spend 1 Cover (Takedown already rolls the die). Cover resets on its own when the scene ends.

Fire Superiority.description:
Spend 3 Hope after you succeed on a weapon attack. Choose one:

  • Add +2d6 to the damage roll.
  • Choose another target within range that your attack roll would also succeed against.
  • The target marks 1 Stress and becomes temporarily Vulnerable.
Marked 1 Stress and became temporarily Vulnerable from Fire Superiority.

Kill Chain.description:
At the beginning of each scene, your Kill Chain Die is a d4. When you succeed on a weapon attack or Assault card that deals damage, roll your Kill Chain Die and add its result to the damage roll.

If the attack deals Major or Severe damage, increase your Kill Chain Die by one step, from d4 up to d20.

If you fail an attack roll, take a rest, or the scene ends, reset your Kill Chain Die to d4.

On the sheet: the die next to this feature shows its current size and last result. Use the actions to roll, increase, or reset it; it goes back to d4 on its own when the scene ends.

Chrome Surge.description:
Spend 3 Hope when you make an Agility, Strength, or Finesse Roll. Roll a d8 and add its result to the roll. If this roll succeeds, choose one:

  • Immediately move within Close range.
  • Clear a Stress.
  • Gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion until your next Spotlight.

On the sheet: the action spends the Hope and rolls the d8 to add to the roll.

Integrated Chrome.description:
Your cyberware is fully integrated into your nervous system. When you finish a rest, choose Agility, Strength, or Finesse as your Calibrated Trait.

When you make an action roll using your Calibrated Trait or use a Chrome card, you can mark a Stress to roll a d6 and add its result to the roll.

Additionally, when you roll your Humanity Die to resist Cyberpsychosis, treat your Cyber Load as 1 lower, to a minimum of 0.

On the sheet: "Calibrate Trait" chooses your Calibrated Trait (shown in the header badge); "Integrated Chrome" marks 1 Stress and rolls the d6. The Humanity Roll already subtracts 1 from your Cyber Load.

pick.title: Calibrated Trait
pick.prompt: Choose your Calibrated Trait until your next rest.

Make It Work.description: Spend 3 Hope after you or an ally within Close range fails an action roll using a device, weapon, or Systems card. Describe your emergency fix, then the target can reroll their Duality Dice and use the new result.

Jury-Rig.description:
Once per scene, when you have a few moments and access to your tools, you can modify, repair, or improvise with a device, weapon, or piece of machinery within Melee range. Choose one:

  • Boost: The next time the modified item is used before the scene ends, add +1d6 to its action roll, Interface Roll, or damage roll.
  • Patch: Restore a broken, jammed, disabled, or damaged item so it functions until the scene ends, or allow a creature using the item to clear an Armor Slot.
  • Rewire: Connect or disconnect the item from a network, bypass its local controls, or allow it to be operated from Far range until the scene ends.

You can mark a Stress to use Jury-Rig again during the same scene.

On the sheet: "Jury-Rig" is the scene's use; "Jury-Rig Extra" marks 1 Stress to use it again; "Roll Boost" rolls the d6 when the modified item is used.

Fine Print.description:
Spend 3 Hope after you or an ally within Far range fails a Presence Roll. Reveal a secret, bribe, threat, or perfect interruption. The failure becomes a success with Fear.

If the failed roll was made directly against a creature, they also mark 1 Stress.

Terms of Engagement.description:
When you succeed on a Presence Roll or Influence card against a creature or group, choose one:

  • Pressure: One affected target marks 1 Stress.
  • Opening: The next action roll made by you or an ally against one affected target gains a +2 bonus.
  • Reassurance: You or an ally within Close range clears 1 Stress.

On a success with Hope, you can mark a Stress to choose one additional option.

On the sheet: each option is an action that records the choice in chat; "Additional Option" marks the Stress.

Opening.description: Opening: The next action roll made by you or an ally against one affected target gains a +2 bonus.

Reassurance.description: Reassurance: You or an ally within Close range clears 1 Stress.

Home Ground.description:
Spend 3 Hope when an adversary within Far range moves, attacks, or targets you or an ally to use the terrain against them. They must make a Reaction Roll (14).

On a failure, they become temporarily Vulnerable or temporarily Restrained and mark 1 Stress. If they are operating a vehicle, you may instead make that vehicle become Damaged. On a success, they mark 1 Stress.

On the sheet: one action for each condition; use the one you choose when the target fails.

Home Ground (Vulnerável).name: Home Ground (Vulnerable)
Home Ground (Vulnerável).description: The terrain turned against them: marked 1 Stress and became temporarily Vulnerable.

Home Ground (Imobilizado).name: Home Ground (Restrained)
Home Ground (Imobilizado).description: The terrain turned against them: marked 1 Stress and became temporarily Restrained.

Surveyed Route.description:
Spend a Hope and take a moment to read the terrain, ruins, or streets around you. Make an Instinct Roll (12). On a success, the area within Far range becomes your Surveyed Route until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. While you are within your Surveyed Route:

  • You and allies within Close range can ignore difficult terrain while moving or driving.
  • When you deal damage to an adversary in the zone, you can force them to mark 1 Stress.
  • When you fail an action roll, you can end your Surveyed Route to reroll your Duality Dice.

Surveyed Route active until the scene ends or you take Severe damage: you and allies within Close range ignore difficult terrain; when you deal damage to an adversary in the zone, you can force them to mark 1 Stress; when you fail an action roll, you can end the Surveyed Route to reroll your Duality Dice.

Stay With Me.description: Spend 3 Hope when a creature within Close range would mark their last unmarked Hit Point or make a Death Move. They don’t take the consequences of the Death Move and remain alive and conscious, clearing 1 Hit Point instead, but become temporarily Vulnerable until they receive medical attention or the scene ends.
Kept alive by Stay With Me: temporarily Vulnerable until receiving medical attention or the scene ends.

Emergency Medicine.description:
When you have a moment to treat a creature within Melee range, make an Interface Roll (12). On a success, choose one:

  • The target clears 1 Stress.
  • The target clears a temporary physical condition, such as Vulnerable or Restrained.
  • The target stabilizes a damaged implant, life-support system, or cyberware component until their next rest.

Once per rest, when you succeed on this roll, the target can clear 1 Hit Point in addition to choosing one of the effects above. A creature can clear a Hit Point from Emergency Medicine only once per rest.

On the sheet: "Emergency Medicine" makes the Interface Roll (12); "Clear 1 HP" tracks the once-per-rest use.

Not Today.description: Spend 3 Hope when an ally within Close range would mark one or more Hit Points. Move to within Very Close range of that ally and reduce the damage severity by one threshold. If this prevents them from marking any Hit Points, you may also clear 1 Stress or force the attacker to mark 1 Stress.

Guardian Protocol.description:
At the end of your Spotlight, choose one ally, vehicle, or objective within Close range as your Guarded Asset until your next Spotlight.

The first attack made against your Guarded Asset before your next Spotlight has disadvantage.

If that attack misses, you may immediately move within Very Close range of the attacker or your Guarded Asset, and the attacker marks 1 Stress.

Guarded Asset.description: Protected by a Warden's Guardian Protocol: the first attack against this target before the Warden's next Spotlight has disadvantage. If that attack misses, the Warden can move within Very Close range of the attacker or the target, and the attacker marks 1 Stress.

Illegal Cyberdeck.description: A custom-built, unlicensed cyberdeck with its own quirks and interface. Describe what it looks like, how old it is, and where you got it.

Stolen Access Shard.description: A physical access shard taken from a job that should have killed you. It still opens something — you just aren’t sure what, or who will notice when it does.

False Credentials.description: A set of false credentials: badge, digital identity, and forged history. Whose face is on the photo, and how long until someone checks?

Suppressed Weapon.description: A suppressed weapon from a job that officially never happened. The serial number was filed off; the memory wasn’t.

Named Custom Weapon.description: A customized weapon with a name. Describe the name, its history, and what you have done with it.

Damaged Dog Tag.description: A damaged dog tag from the fight that made your reputation. Whose name is stamped on it?

Implant Maintenance Kit.description: A maintenance kit for your most important implant: precision drivers, conductive gel, spare parts, and a manual full of your own notes.

Original Body Part.description: The original piece of your body that was replaced by chrome. Why do you still keep it?

Custom Toolkit.description: A customized toolkit full of illegal adapters and scavenged parts. You made half of the tools yourself.

Broken Machine.description: A broken machine you refuse to stop repairing. What was it, and why does it matter so much?

Contact List.description: A contact list worth more than your bank balance. Who is at the top of it, and who was crossed out?

Contract Chip.description: A contract chip containing a big and illegal corporate deal. Who would pay to have it, and who would kill to erase it?

Cracked Route-Map.description: A cracked route-map filled with personal markings: shortcuts, hideouts, dead zones, and names only you understand.

Piece of Salvage.description: A piece of salvage from the place that should have killed you. You carry it to remember that you got out.

Trauma Kit.description: A trauma kit full of illegal pharmaceuticals and tools. Half of it has no record; the other half was registered under someone else’s name.

Patient Tag.description: The bloodstained patient tag of someone you could not save. You still remember the name.

Marked Defensive Rig.description: A defensive rig marked by old impacts. Every dent tells the story of someone who didn’t get hurt because you were in front.

Contract Token.description: A contract token from someone you swore to protect. The contract may be over; the promise isn’t.

Breach Specialist.description:
Play as a Breach Specialist if you want to weaponize intrusion, break enemy systems, crash defenses, and turn networks into attack vectors.

Suggested Build: Knowledge +2, Agility +1, Instinct +1, Presence 0, Strength 0, Finesse −1. Recommended equipment: Scrap Launcher (primary, two-handed — no secondary weapon) + Ballistic Vest — suited to direct assaults on systems and to surviving the melee range Rootkill pulls you into.

Net Diver.description:
Play as a Net Diver if you want to enter hostile networks, control connected systems, and complete the job from inside the digital architecture.

Suggested Build: Instinct +2, Finesse +1, Agility +1, Presence 0, Knowledge 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Smartbow (primary, two-handed — no secondary weapon) + Synthleather Jacket — suited to staying mobile and covering allies from range while in a Deep Dive.

Silent Killer.description:
Play as a Silent Killer if you want to eliminate targets with precision and end fights before they begin.

Suggested Build: Finesse +2, Agility +1, Instinct +1, Presence 0, Knowledge 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Mono-Katana (primary, one-handed) + Combat Knife (secondary) + Synthleather Jacket — close attacks, striking from Hidden.

Phantom.description:
Play as a Phantom if you want to slip through guarded spaces, reposition through blind spots, extract allies from danger, and disappear before the enemy can lock you down.

(The PDF's subclass list calls this one "Deep Cover", but its section is named Phantom.)

Suggested Build: Agility +2, Finesse +1, Instinct +1, Presence 0, Knowledge 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Compact SMG (primary, one-handed) + Combat Knife (secondary) + Synthleather Jacket — mobility and high Evasion.

Deadeye.description:
Play as a Deadeye if you want to eliminate priority targets, exploit openings, and make every shot count.

Suggested Build: Finesse +2, Agility +1, Instinct +1, Strength 0, Presence 0, Knowledge −1. Recommended equipment: Smartbow (primary, two-handed) + Synthleather Jacket — attacks from range, staying still to use the bow's Draw.

Shock Trooper.description:
Play as a Shock Trooper if you want to breach fortified positions, fight up close, break enemy lines, and keep moving through danger.

Suggested Build: Strength +2, Agility +1, Instinct +1, Finesse 0, Presence 0, Knowledge −1. Recommended equipment: Street Shotgun (primary, two-handed) + Ballistic Vest — close combat, moving into Very Close range for Hard Entry.

Reflex Suite.description:
Play as a Reflex Suite if you want to move faster than human reaction time and turn your nervous system into a weapon.

Suggested Build: Agility +2, Finesse +1, Instinct +1, Strength 0, Presence 0, Knowledge −1. Recommended equipment: Compact SMG (primary, one-handed) + Combat Knife (secondary) + Synthleather Jacket — high Evasion and calibrated Agility.

Titan Frame.description:
Play as a Titan Frame if you want to become a mountain of heavy chrome and industrial strength that refuses to move unless you allow it.

Suggested Build: Strength +2, Agility +1, Instinct +1, Finesse 0, Presence 0, Knowledge −1. Recommended equipment: Breach Hammer (primary, two-handed) + Ballistic Vest — Strength calibrated for Reinforced Build.

Rigger.description:
Play as a Rigger if you want to control drones, operate machines remotely, and support allies through equipment.

Suggested Build: Knowledge +2, Agility +1, Instinct +1, Finesse 0, Presence 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Scrap Launcher (primary, two-handed) + Ballistic Vest — the drone does the close work while you stay at Close range.

Saboteur.description:
Play as a Saboteur if you want to plant charges, disable defenses, and turn the environment against your enemies.

Suggested Build: Finesse +2, Knowledge +1, Agility +1, Instinct 0, Presence 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Mono-Katana (primary, one-handed) + Grapple Wire (secondary) + Synthleather Jacket — getting close to plant charges.

Fixer.description:
Play as a Fixer if you want to arrange jobs, call in favors, and navigate the city’s hidden economy.

Suggested Build: Presence +2, Knowledge +1, Instinct +1, Agility 0, Finesse 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Shock Baton (primary, one-handed) + Shock Glove (secondary) + Synthleather Jacket — both weapons use Presence.

Icon.description:
Play as an Icon if you want to weaponize reputation, performance, fame, fear, propaganda, and public perception.

Suggested Build: Presence +2, Agility +1, Finesse +1, Instinct 0, Knowledge 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Shock Baton (primary, one-handed) + Shock Glove (secondary) + Street Icon Fit — reputation is part of the outfit.

Outrider.description:
Play as an Outrider if you want to master vehicles, lead pursuits, and survive impossible roads.

Suggested Build: Agility +2, Instinct +1, Finesse +1, Strength 0, Presence 0, Knowledge −1. Recommended equipment: Assault Carbine (primary, two-handed) + Synthleather Jacket — shooting from range, from inside the vehicle.

Zonebreaker.description:
Play as a Zonebreaker if you want to dominate terrain, turn ruins into weapons, and make the battlefield itself dangerous.

Suggested Build: Instinct +2, Agility +1, Strength +1, Finesse 0, Knowledge 0, Presence −1. Recommended equipment: Compact SMG (primary, one-handed) + Tactical Drone (secondary, Instinct) + Ballistic Vest — staying inside the Surveyed Route and holding position.

Combat Medic.description:
Play as a Combat Medic if you want to keep the crew alive and perform emergency treatment in the middle of combat.

Suggested Build: Instinct +2, Agility +1, Knowledge +1, Finesse 0, Presence 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Compact SMG (primary, one-handed) + Tactical Drone (secondary, Instinct) + Ballistic Vest — mobility to reach whoever went down.

Street Surgeon.description:
Play as a Street Surgeon if you want to use illegal medicine, cyberware patches, black-clinic procedures, and dangerous stimulants to push bodies past safe limits.

Suggested Build: Knowledge +2, Finesse +1, Instinct +1, Agility 0, Presence 0, Strength −1. Recommended equipment: Scrap Launcher (primary, two-handed, Knowledge) + Synthleather Jacket — the same trait for attacks and protocols.

Bulwark.description:
Play as a Bulwark if you want to become heavy armor, riot shielding, and the person enemies regret hitting.

Suggested Build: Strength +2, Instinct +1, Presence +1, Agility 0, Knowledge 0, Finesse −1. Recommended equipment: Breach Hammer (primary, two-handed) + Riot Shell — the heaviest Tier 1 armor, to get the most out of Impact Frame.

Riotbreaker.description:
Play as a Riotbreaker if you want to break charges, control space, shove enemies around, and turn defense into force.

Suggested Build: Presence +2, Strength +1, Instinct +1, Agility 0, Knowledge 0, Finesse −1. Recommended equipment: Shock Baton (primary, one-handed) + Riot Buckler (secondary) + Riot Shell — close control with a free hand for the shield.

Exploit Payload.description: When you Exploit a creature, drone, vehicle, or connected system, you can mark a Stress to make the target temporarily Vulnerable.

Hard Crash.description: Once per rest, when you create a Breach against a target you have Exploited, you can immediately use that Breach without spending it.

Cascade Breach.description: Once per scene, when you create a Breach, you can immediately create another Breach on a connected target or system within Close range of the original target.

Rootkill.description: Once per long rest, when you successfully Hack a target you have Exploited, you can force a catastrophic system failure. The target marks 1 Stress and 1 Hit Point, then becomes temporarily Degraded. While Degraded, the target uses a d12 instead of a d20 for attack rolls.

Degraded.description: While Degraded, the target uses a d12 instead of a d20 for attack rolls.

Deep Dive.description: Once per scene, when you create a Breach in a network, you can enter a Deep Dive. While in a Deep Dive: you can interact with connected systems in the scene regardless of range; you gain a bonus equal to your Tier on Interface Rolls involving Hacking or Network cards; you can ask the GM one question about the network, its security, connected systems, or hidden routes. The Deep Dive ends when you take Major damage, disconnect, or the scene ends.
Interact with connected systems in the scene regardless of range; +Tier on Hacking Interface Rolls or Network cards. Ends when you take Major damage, disconnect, or the scene ends.

Virtual Overwatch.description: When an adversary targets you or an ally within Very Close range with an attack while you are in a Deep Dive, you can give them disadvantage on the roll. If the adversary fails the roll, they must also mark a Stress. If they succeed, you must mark a Stress.

Blackout Cascade.description: Once per long rest, while in a Deep Dive, you can trigger a massive network disruption. Choose up to three connected systems, devices, or cyberware-linked targets in the scene. For each one, choose one: Disable it until the GM spends a Fear; Feed it false information, giving disadvantage on its next roll; Overload it, causing its operator to mark 1 Stress; Open, lock, jam, redirect, control, or trigger it in a way that significantly changes the scene. Afterward, mark a Stress or become temporarily Vulnerable.

Opening Strike.description:
Once per Spotlight, when you deal damage to a target while you are Hidden from them or while they are Vulnerable, add a number of d6s equal to your Tier to the damage roll.

On the sheet: the action rolls the d6s for your Tier to add to the damage.

No Witnesses.description: When you defeat or disable a target with an attack you made while Hidden, you can immediately become Hidden again and move to a point within Very Close range.

Kill Window.description: When you spend Cover on Takedown, you roll a d8 instead of a d6. Additionally, if the target is Vulnerable, they must also mark a Stress.

Perfect Ambush.description:
Once per long rest, when you make a successful attack against a target you are Hidden from, do not roll your weapon damage dice. Instead, use the highest possible value of those dice.

If the target survives the attack, they become permanently Vulnerable.
Survived a Perfect Ambush and became permanently Vulnerable.

Ghost Route.description:
When you move while Hidden, you can move within Far range instead of Close range.

If you start this movement within Very Close range of an ally, you can bring them with you. That ally doesn’t become Hidden unless they were already Hidden.

Now You See Me.description: Once per scene, when an attack against you misses or has disadvantage, you can gain 1 Cover.

Extraction Window.description:
When an ally within Close range would be targeted by an attack, discovered, or caught by a danger, you can spend 1 Cover to make that ally immediately move to a point within Close range.

The triggering attack has disadvantage against them, or the ally has advantage on the roll to avoid it.

Impossible Exit.description:
Once per rest, you can spend 3 Cover to reveal an escape route you prepared or noticed. You and any allies within Close range can immediately move within Far range, ignoring difficult terrain, simple alarms, and zones controlled by enemies during this movement.

After this movement, you become Hidden. Any ally who ends this movement in cover, darkness, smoke, a crowd, or another plausible hiding place also becomes Hidden.

Marked Target.description:
Once per rest, when you deal damage to a target, you can mark them as your priority target until the scene ends or you mark another target this way.

When you roll your Kill Chain Die against your marked target, you can reroll the die and use either result.
The Deadeye's priority target until the scene ends or another target is marked. When rolling the Kill Chain Die against it, the Deadeye can reroll and use either result.

Called Shot.description:
When you make a weapon attack against your marked target, you can mark a Stress before the roll to gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll.

If the attack succeeds and deals any damage, increase your Kill Chain Die by one step, even if the attack did not deal Major or Severe damage.

Kill Confirmed.description:
Once per long rest, when you deal Severe damage to your marked target, they must mark an additional Hit Point.

If this defeats them, you can immediately mark a new target as your marked target and set your Kill Chain Die to d10.

Breach Momentum.description: When your Kill Chain Die increases, gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion until your next action.

Hard Entry.description: When you make an attack immediately after moving into Melee or Very Close range of your target, you can mark a Stress to add your Kill Chain Die to the damage roll again.

Clear the Line.description:
Once per rest, when you deal Major or Severe damage to an adversary within Melee or Very Close range, you can force them and each adversary within Very Close range of them to mark 1 Stress.

Then choose one affected adversary and make them temporarily Vulnerable.

No Way Back.description:
Once per long rest, when you enter a dangerous fight, set your Kill Chain Die to d10.

Until the scene ends or you take Severe damage, your Kill Chain Die does not reset when you fail an attack roll.

While this feature is active, you can’t willingly move away from all adversaries unless an ally is in immediate danger.

Kill Chain Die at d10; until the scene ends or you take Severe damage, it doesn't reset when you fail an attack. You can't willingly move away from all adversaries unless an ally is in immediate danger.

Neural Reflexes.description: When you use Integrated Chrome on an Agility or Finesse Roll, you can immediately move within Very Close range after the roll resolves. If that roll succeeds with Hope, you can move within Close range instead.

Fast Enough.description: Once per rest, when an attack against you would hit, you can mark a Stress to roll a d6 and add its result to your Evasion against that attack.

Motion Blur.description: When you move within Close range or farther during your Spotlight, the next attack made against you before your next Spotlight has disadvantage.

Accelerated Loop.description: Once per long rest, you can push your reflexware into full acceleration. Until the scene ends or you take Severe damage, the first time each Spotlight that you use Integrated Chrome on a successful Agility or Finesse Roll, you can clear a Stress or immediately move within Very Close range.

Reflexware in full acceleration until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. The first time each Spotlight you use Integrated Chrome on a successful Agility or Finesse Roll, clear 1 Stress or move within Very Close range.

Reinforced Build.description:
When your Calibrated Trait is Strength, gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Score. Additionally, when you use Integrated Chrome on a Strength Roll, roll a d8 instead of a d6.

On the sheet: the +1 Armor turns on by itself when you calibrate Strength and off for the other traits.
+1 Armor Score while your Calibrated Trait is Strength.

Load-Bearing Body.description: You have advantage on rolls to resist being pushed, knocked down, disarmed, moved against your will, or temporarily Restrained.

Impact Absorbers.description:
Once per scene, when you would mark one or more Hit Points from physical or impact damage, you can mark a Stress to reduce the severity by one threshold.

If this prevents you from marking any Hit Points, you can immediately move within Very Close range or force the attacker to mark 1 Stress.

Heavy Chrome Walking.description:
Once per long rest, when you mark an Armor Slot, you can activate your full-body reinforcement until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. While this feature is active:

  • When you make a successful Melee attack roll, you can add your Calibrated Trait die to the damage roll.
  • Gain a +3 bonus to your damage thresholds.
  • When you succeed on a Strength Roll or weapon attack against a target within Melee range, you can push them back to Close range and make them temporarily Vulnerable.

Full-body reinforcement active until the scene ends or you take Severe damage: +3 to damage thresholds; on Melee attacks, add your Calibrated Trait die to damage; when you succeed on a Strength Roll or attack against a Melee target, you can push them to Close range and make them temporarily Vulnerable.

Companion Drone.description:
You have a small drone or machine companion that can move independently within Far range, carry small objects, record, scan, and interact with controls.

You may Help an ally within Close range of the drone regardless of your own position. If their roll involves equipment or connected systems, use a d8 as your Help die.

When the drone would take damage, mark a Stress to move it out of danger. Otherwise, it is disabled until your next rest.

On the sheet: "Drone Help" spends 1 Hope and rolls the d8 Help die; "Protect Drone" marks 1 Stress.

Remote Hands.description: You may use Jury-Rig through your drone as though you were touching the target. After using Boost or Patch, the drone may immediately move within Close range.

Drone Network.description:
Once per long rest, deploy a drone network until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. While active:

  • Your drone can operate within Very Far range.
  • Jury-Rig used through it may apply two effects.
  • When an ally within Close range of it takes damage, mark a Stress to reduce that damage by 1d8.

Drone network active until the scene ends or you take Severe damage: the drone operates within Very Far range, Jury-Rig used through it applies two effects, and you can mark 1 Stress to reduce by 1d8 the damage taken by an ally within Close range of the drone.

Planted Charge.description:
When you can touch an object, surface, or machine, mark a Stress to plant a charge. Trigger it later in the scene to choose one:

  • Breach: Open, break, or collapse the target.
  • Disable: Jam, lock, or shut it down until repaired.
  • Disrupt: One adversary within Very Close range marks 1 Stress and becomes temporarily Vulnerable.

You can have one active charge at a time.

Disrupt.description: Marked 1 Stress and became temporarily Vulnerable from a charge (Disrupt).

Cascading Failure.description:
You can have two active charges. When one is triggered:

  • Breach: You or an ally Close to it may immediately move within Close range.
  • Disable: An adversary using the target also marks 1 Stress.
  • Disrupt: The affected adversary has disadvantage on their next action roll before your next Spotlight.

Controlled Demolition.description:
Once per long rest, when you trigger a charge, destroy, collapse, open, or disable its target to create a major breach, escape route, or obstruction.

Adversaries within Close range make a Reaction Roll (16). On a failure, they take 3d10 physical damage and become temporarily Restrained. On a success, they take half damage.

On the sheet: the action rolls the 3d10 and applies Restrained to targets who fail.
Caught by the controlled demolition: temporarily Restrained.

Black-Market Network.description:
Once per rest in a populated area, declare that you know a contact who can provide restricted gear, shelter, transportation, information, or access to someone difficult to reach. The GM tells you what they want in return.

When you or an ally uses the contact’s help, gain +2 to one relevant action roll.

Contacts Everywhere.description:
Once per rest, call in immediate help from a contact. Describe how the contact intervenes and choose one:

  • Reduce the Hit Points marked by you or an ally by 1.
  • Gain +3 to your next action roll.
  • Add 2d8 to your next damage roll.

On the sheet: "Roll 2d8" rolls the extra damage from the third option.

Everybody Owes Somebody.description:
Once per long rest, ask the GM who in the scene can be bought, pressured, or turned. Your first Presence Roll or Influence card against them has advantage.

On a success, choose two options from Terms of Engagement instead of one.

Public Persona.description:
Choose what your name means on the street:

  • Beloved: When you use Terms of Engagement to let yourself or an ally clear Stress, that target clears 2 Stress instead.
  • Feared: When you use Terms of Engagement to make a target mark Stress, you can mark a Stress to make them temporarily Vulnerable.
  • Famous: When you use Terms of Engagement to grant a +2 bonus to a roll, grant a +4 bonus to the roll instead.

You can change your Public Persona when you take a long rest and explain how your image shifts.

On the sheet: "Choose Public Persona" stores the choice, shown in the header badge.

pick.title: Public Persona
pick.prompt: Choose what your name means on the street (changes on a long rest).

Live Feed.description:
Once per rest, when you make a successful Presence Roll or use an Influence card while being watched by a crowd, recorded, or streamed by a group, you can amplify the moment.

Choose any number of creatures within Close range who can see or hear you. Allies clear 1 Stress. Adversaries must mark 1 Stress.

Living Brand.description:
Once per long rest, you can step fully into your reputation until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. While this feature is active, the first time each Spotlight that you succeed on a Presence Roll or with an Influence card, choose one:

  • An ally who can see or hear you gains a Hope.
  • An adversary who can see or hear you marks 1 Stress.
  • You clear 1 Stress.

Reputation fully embraced until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. The first time each Spotlight you succeed on a Presence Roll or Influence card: an ally gains 1 Hope, an adversary marks 1 Stress, or you clear 1 Stress.

Signature Vehicle.description:
You have a personal vehicle. When operating it, you may use Agility instead of its listed Trait.

Once per scene, prevent your Signature Vehicle from becoming Damaged or from becoming Disabled. You may designate a new Signature Vehicle during a rest.

Stunt Driver.description:
Once per scene while operating your Signature Vehicle, describe a stunt and make an Agility Roll (15). On a success, choose two. On a failure, choose one, then your vehicle becomes Damaged or you mark 1 Stress.

  • Move within Far range.
  • Give one ally +2 to their next action roll.
  • Make one adversary mark 1 Stress.

Drive Off.description:
Once per long rest, when you succeed on a driving roll with your Signature Vehicle, you may move within Far range or clear 1 Stress.

Additionally, one adversary makes a Reaction Roll (16). On a failure, it takes 3d10 physical damage and becomes temporarily Vulnerable. On a success, it takes half damage.

On the sheet: the action rolls the 3d10 and makes the target Vulnerable if it fails.

Field Salvage.description:
Once per scene, you can scavenge useful material from the surrounding area. Choose one piece of Field Salvage:

  • Patch: You or an ally within Melee range clears an Armor Slot.
  • Tool: You or an ally gains a +2 bonus to their next action.
  • Hazard: The next time you deal damage to an adversary within your Surveyed Route, add 1d6 physical damage to the damage roll.

Unused Field Salvage is lost when you take a rest.

On the sheet: "Field Salvage" tracks the scene's use; "Roll Hazard" rolls the d6.

Bad Ground.description:
