Once per rest, when an adversary inside your Surveyed Route moves within Close range or farther, you can describe how the terrain turns against them. They must make a Reaction Roll (15).

On a failure, the adversary becomes temporarily Restrained, or a vehicle becomes Damaged, and they mark 1 Stress. On a success, they mark 1 Stress.
The terrain turned against them: marked 1 Stress and became temporarily Restrained.

Dead Zone.description:
Once per long rest, when you create a Surveyed Route, you can turn it into a Dead Zone until the scene ends or you take Severe damage. While inside your Dead Zone:

  • Adversaries that move within Very Close range of you must mark a Stress.
  • Adversaries treat the entire area as difficult terrain.
  • When you deal damage to an adversary in the Dead Zone, add 1d8 physical damage to the damage roll.

Dead Zone active until the scene ends or you take Severe damage: adversaries that move within Very Close range of you mark 1 Stress; adversaries treat the area as difficult terrain; when you deal damage to an adversary in the zone, add 1d8 physical damage.

Rapid Response.description: When an ally within Close range marks one or more Hit Points, you can mark a Stress to immediately move to within Melee range of them. The next time you use Emergency Medicine on that ally before the scene ends, you roll with advantage.

Field Extraction.description: When you successfully use Emergency Medicine on a creature, you can immediately move them within Very Close range. This movement can place them behind cover, out of immediate danger, or away from enemy vision.

Mass Casualty Protocol.description: Once per rest, when you successfully use Emergency Medicine, you can also treat a second creature within Very Close range of the original target.

Combat Triage.description:
Once per long rest, when a dangerous scene begins or when an ally within Far range marks one or more Hit Points, you can call a triage order. Choose up to three allies within Far range who can hear you, see you, or receive your signal. Each chosen ally may immediately move within Very Close range, then choose one:

  • Clear 1 Hit Point and 1 Stress.
  • Clear a temporary physical condition.
  • Gain a +2 bonus to their next roll.

Black-Clinic Procedure.description:
When you successfully use Emergency Medicine on a creature, you can give them a dangerous enhancement in addition to the normal effect. Choose one:

  • They add 1d8 to their next damage roll.
  • They gain a +2 bonus to their next Agility, Strength, or Finesse Roll.
  • They gain a +2 bonus to Evasion against the next attack that targets them.

After the enhanced roll or effect resolves, they mark 1 Stress.

On the sheet: "Roll 1d8" rolls the extra damage from the first option.

Bad Medicine.description:
Once per rest, when you succeed on a Medtech card, weapon attack, or Interface Roll against an adversary within Close range, you can turn your medical expertise against them.

The target marks 1 Stress. The next time that target deals damage, reduce the damage by 1 Hit Point.

Miracle Cocktail.description:
Once per long rest, when you successfully use Emergency Medicine on a creature, you can flood their body with illegal stabilizers, combat drugs, nerve blockers, or emergency cyberware commands.

In addition to the normal benefits of Emergency Medicine, the target may immediately move within Close range and make one action roll with advantage. If this action deals damage, add 2d8 to the damage roll.

On the sheet: the action tracks the use and rolls the 2d8.

Impact Frame.description:
Gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Score.

When you mark an Armor Slot to reduce incoming damage, you may force the attacker to mark 1 Stress or push them back to Close range, the attacker’s choice.

Hard to Break.description: Once per rest, when you would mark one or more Hit Points, you can mark a Stress to reduce the severity by one threshold.

Unbreakable Frame.description:
Once per long rest, when you mark an Armor Slot, you can activate your full defensive rig until the scene ends or you mark your last Armor Slot. While this feature is active, when you mark an Armor Slot, choose one:

  • Clear 1 Stress.
  • Force the attacker to mark 1 Stress.
  • One ally within Very Close range gains a +1 bonus to Evasion until your next Spotlight.

Full defensive rig active until the scene ends or you mark your last Armor Slot. When you mark an Armor Slot, choose: clear 1 Stress; force the attacker to mark 1 Stress; or one ally within Very Close range gains +1 Evasion until your next Spotlight.

Crowd Control.description:
When you succeed on a weapon attack or Aegis card, choose one adversary within Close range. Until your next Spotlight, that adversary can’t willingly move closer to one ally, objective, or position you choose unless they first mark 1 Stress.

If the target is already within Very Close range of the protected ally, objective, or position, they must immediately move away to Close range or mark 1 Stress.

Hard Stop.description:
Once per rest, when an adversary within Close range moves toward you or an ally, force them to make a Reaction Roll (15).

On a failure, they stop moving and become temporarily Restrained.

On a success, they mark 1 Stress.

Break the Line.description:
Once per long rest, when you enter the center of a dangerous fight, choose any number of adversaries within Close range. Each chosen adversary must make a Reaction Roll (16).

On a failure, they are pushed back to Close range and become temporarily Vulnerable.

On a success, they mark 1 Stress.
Pushed back to Close range and temporarily Vulnerable.

Corpo-Raised.description: You were raised inside corporate structure. You understand polished violence, contracts, etiquette, artificial comfort, and the language of people who believe they own the future.

Corporate Design.description: Choose one of your Experiences tied to corporate training, education, etiquette, security, finance, or bureaucracy. Gain a permanent +1 bonus to it.

Efficient Routine.description: When you take a short rest, you can choose one long rest move instead of one short rest move.

Streetborn.description: You grew up in the streets, alleys, and gang districts of the New Dark Age. You learned how to read danger before it speaks.

Alley Reflexes.description: When you make an Agility Roll, you can spend 2 Hope to reroll your Hope Die.

Re-rolar Dado de Esperança.name: Reroll Hope Die
Re-rolar Dado de Esperança.description: Reroll your Hope Die on an Agility Roll.

Cheap Shot.description: When you succeed on an attack against a target within Very Close range using an improvised weapon, hidden blade, dirty trick, or street tactic, you can spend a Hope to make them temporarily Vulnerable.

Nomad.description: You come from road clans, convoy families, or people who survived by never staying owned. You know engines, routes, and the value of family chosen at road.

Road Sprint.description: When you succeed on an Agility Roll or vehicle roll to move from Far or Very Far range into Melee range with one or more targets, you can mark a Stress to deal 1d12 physical damage to all targets within Melee range.

Off-Road Born.description: You can move naturally through rubble, broken roads, mud, sand, shallow water, wreckage, and unstable ground.

Military Surplus.description: You were trained by a corporate army, gang warband, or collapsed national force. Maybe you deserted. Maybe your unit was sold. Maybe you are the only one left.

Combat Reactions.description: Mark a Stress to gain advantage on a Reaction Roll.
Gain advantage on your next Reaction Roll.

Last One Standing.description: When you have 1 Hit Point remaining, attacks against you have disadvantage.

Black-Clinic Survivor.description: You were rebuilt in an illegal clinic, experimental trauma ward, chop shop, organ market, cyberware den, or emergency surgical pit. Your body carries the price of survival.

Scar Tissue.description: When you would mark a Hit Point or Stress from physical damage, roll a d6. On a 6, don’t mark it.

Emergency Rebuild.description: When you would take Severe damage, you can mark a Stress to mark 1 fewer Hit Point.

Wasteland Native.description: You come from a dead zone or place the city pretends does not exist. You know that survival is not luck. It is attention.

Hazard-Bred.description: You can breathe, move, and act naturally in smoke, ash, dust, polluted air, shallow water, heavy rain, toxic stink, or unstable terrain unless it is immediately lethal.

Hard as Nails.description: Gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to your Proficiency.
Gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to your Proficiency.

Corporate Asset.description: You are connected to a corporation as an employee, sponsored mercenary, or former insider.

Elite Privilege.description: You have advantage on rolls to consort with corporate employees, pass as authorized, or leverage your company reputation to get what you want.

Gang-Tied.description: You are connected to a gang, street family, or violent local power.

Street Wise.description: You have advantage on rolls to negotiate with criminals, detect lies, recognize gang signs, or find a safe place to hide in criminal territory.

Nomad Convoy.description: You are connected to a convoy, road clan, or wasteland route.

Law of the Road.description: Record three rules, codes, or protocols your convoy drilled into you. Once per rest, when you describe how you’re embodying one of these principles through your current action, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

Mercenary Network.description: You are connected to a mercenary company, job board, or professional network of hired guns.

Unbound.description: Once per session, when you make an action roll with Fear, you can change it to a roll with Hope instead.

Black Clinic.description: You are connected to a street doctor, illegal clinic, or illegal cyberware medical ring.

Chillax.description: During a short rest, you or an ally can reroll a die used for a recovery, repair, or cyberware-related downtime action.

Fixer Network.description: You are connected to information sellers, job handlers, and people who know a person who knows a person.

Know the Deal.description: You have a sixth sense for dealing with the uncertainties of your profession. When you roll with Fear, place a token on this Affiliation. You can hold a number of tokens equal to your level. Before you make an action roll, you can spend any number of these tokens to gain a +1 bonus to the roll for each token spent. At the end of each session, clear all unspent tokens.

Resistance Cell.description: You are connected to rebels, labor organizers, or anti-corporate cells.

Found Family.description: Once per session, you can spend a Hope to use an ally’s Affiliation Feature. When you do, your ally gains a Hope.

Data Cult.description: You are connected to digital mystics, Old Net scavengers, Blackwall obsessives, rogue archivists, signal prophets, or people who believe the machine is haunted.

Forbidden Pattern.description: Your connection to corrupted data, rogue AI signs, Blackwall residue, impossible signals, or lost technology might have altered your perception of reality. You can spend 2 Hope to reroll your Fear Die.

Neon Claw Ganger.description: A loud ganger with cheap chrome, bright colors, and something to prove.

Minion (3).description: The @Lookup[@name] is defeated when they take any damage. For every 3 damage a PC deals to the @Lookup[@name], defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Group Attack.description: Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all @Lookup[@name]s within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal @Lookup[@system.attack.damageFormula] physical damage each. Combine this damage.

Show of Force.description: When another gang ally within Close range deals damage, this Ganger may immediately move within Very Close range of the damaged target.

Sitil Security Guard.description: A private security guard trained to delay intruders until the real deal arrives.

Badge Discipline.description: While within Close range of a corporate device, checkpoint, camera, or locked door, this adversary gains +1 Difficulty.
+1 Difficulty. Turn it on while the guard is near a corporate device, checkpoint, camera, or locked door.

Call It In.description: Mark a Stress to activate local security. The next corporate adversary spotlighted gains advantage on their action roll.

Chrome Maw Bruiser.description: A gang enforcer with reinforced jaws, hydraulic arms, and a body built for intimidation.

Chrome Bulk.description: The first time this adversary would mark HP, they may mark a Stress instead.

Jawbreaker.description: Mark a Stress to attack a target within Melee range. On a success, the target must mark a Stress or become temporarily Vulnerable.

Tiger Choir Cutter.description: A masked blade who moves through crowds like a rumor with a knife.

Crowd Slip.description: When spotlighted in a crowd, club, market, alley, or chaotic street, this adversary becomes Hidden until it acts.

Reputation Cut.description: Mark a Stress to attack a target within Melee range. On a success, deal damage and the target cannot spend Hope until the Cutter’s next Spotlight.
Cannot spend Hope until the Tiger Choir Cutter's next Spotlight.

Pocket Drone Handler.description: A nervous operator surrounded by cheap combat drones and too many screens.
Pocket Drone Handler.motivesAndTactics: Mark targets, hide behind machines, call signals

Spotter Swarm.description: The first corporate or gang ally to attack a target damaged by this adversary gains +1 to the attack roll.

Send the Drone.description: Mark a Stress to move a drone anywhere within Far range. A target within Very Close range of the drone must make an Agility Reaction Roll or take 1d6+2 techno damage and mark a Stress.

Rookie Edgerunner.description: A young mercenary with rented gear, real ambition, and bad judgment.
Rookie Edgerunner.motivesAndTactics: Take cover, show off, survive the job

Cover Shooter.description: While behind cover, this adversary gains +1 Difficulty.
+1 Difficulty. Turn it on while the Rookie is behind cover.

Panic Burst.description: When this adversary marks HP, they may mark a Stress to immediately make a standard attack with disadvantage.

Blood Saint Duelist.description: A stylish street killer who treats every fight like a public performance.

Witness Me.description: If a PC rolls with Fear within Close range of this adversary, the Duelist gains advantage on their next attack.

Signature Cut.description: Mark a Stress to attack a Vulnerable target. On a success, deal damage and the target must mark 1 Stress.

Public Humiliation.description: When this adversary deals Major or Severe damage, choose one PC within Close range who saw it happen. They must lose 1 Hope or become Vulnerable.
Temporarily Vulnerable from the Duelist's public humiliation.

Korvax Neural Interrogator.description: A corporate mind-tech specialist who turns fears and memory into weapons.

Legal Threat.description: PCs within Close range have disadvantage on rolls to lie, negotiate, or conceal information while under direct questioning.
Disadvantage on rolls to lie, negotiate, or conceal information while under direct questioning.

Memory Hook.description: Mark a Stress. One target within Close range must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, they mark 2 Stress. On a success, they mark 1 Stress.

Pressure File.description: When a PC rolls with Fear on a social, hacking, or investigation roll, reveal that Korvax already has leverage on them, their crew, their contacts, or their cyberware. The PC marks 1 Stress.

Corporate Response Team.description: A disciplined tactical unit moving under drone overwatch and helmet-to-helmet command.

Horde (1d6+2).description: When the @Lookup[@name] has marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals @Lookup[@system.typeData.hordeDamage] physical damage instead.

Stack Up.description: Mark a Stress to move within Close range and attack. On a success, the target is pushed back to Close range or marks 1 Stress.

Tactical Sweep.description: When a PC rolls with Fear while Hidden, behind cover, or inside a secured area, this Horde immediately identifies their position and one corporate ally gains advantage against them.

Black-Clinic Butcher.description: A back-alley surgeon turned combat freak, carrying tools meant for bodies that are still screaming.

Pain Map.description: When this adversary deals damage to a target who has marked HP, that target also marks 1 Stress.

Surgical Disable.description: Mark a Stress to attack a target within Melee range. On a success, deal damage and temporarily disable one of the target's cyberware.

Emergency Stitching.description: When this adversary would mark HP, they may mark 2 Stress instead.

Contract Sniper.description: A patient killer hired to end the job before the crew even reaches the door.

Prepared Position.description: This adversary starts a scene Hidden. The first time this adversary attacks while Hidden, add +1d8 damage.

Marked Shot.description: Mark a Stress and choose one target within Very Far range. The next attack this adversary makes against that target gains a +2 bonus to the attack roll.
In the Contract Sniper's sights: their next attack against this target gains +2.

Relocate.description: When a PC rolls with Fear against this adversary, the Sniper becomes Hidden if there’s no PC within Very Close range of it.

Signal Haunt.description: A corrupted AI presence flickering through cameras, implants, headlights, and dead screens.

Augmented Haunting.description: PCs using cyberware, connected gear, or sensors within Close range have disadvantage on rolls to distinguish real threats from false signals.
Disadvantage on rolls to distinguish real threats from false signals.

Signal Spike.description: Mark a Stress and choose one PC within Far range using connected gear, cyberware, sensors, or comms. They must mark 1 Stress or lose the benefit of that system until they spend a Hope to re-enable it.
Lost the benefit of a connected system (gear, cyberware, sensors, or comms) until spending 1 Hope to re-enable it.

Hostile Overlay.description: When a PC within Far range rolls with Fear, mark a Stress to corrupt their interface. Their vision or sensors fill with hostile markers and false warnings. They become Vulnerable until they mark 1 Stress to tear through the signal.
The interface is corrupted by hostile markers and false warnings: Vulnerable until marking 1 Stress to tear through the signal.

Sitil Black-Ops Captain.description: A corporate commander with encrypted orders and permission to erase witnesses.

Operational Control.description: Corporate allies within Close range gain +1 Difficulty.
+1 Difficulty from the Sitil Black-Ops Captain's command.

Kill Order.description: Mark a Stress. The captain and one corporate ally within Far range immediately move within Very Close range and make a standard attack.

No Witnesses.description: Mark 2 Stress and choose one object, body, terminal, witness, camera, or piece of evidence within Far range. It is destroyed, erased, extracted, or placed in immediate danger. If it chooses a target, it becomes Marked. Corporate allies that attack a Marked target have advantage against it.

Marked.description: Marked by Sitil: corporate allies have advantage on attacks against this target.

Asset Denial.description: When a PC rolls with Fear, lock down one door, route, elevator, drone, or security system within Far range.

Rival Edgerunner Crew.description: A full mercenary crew moving with rehearsed roles, inside jokes, and a shared objective.
Rival Edgerunner Crew.motivesAndTactics: Outmaneuver, steal objective, cover each other

Horde (2d6+4).description: When the @Lookup[@name] has marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals @Lookup[@system.typeData.hordeDamage] physical damage instead.

Role Switch.description: When this adversary takes the Spotlight, choose one, or mark a Stress to choose two: gain +2 Difficulty; deal +1d8 damage; clear 1 Stress.

Setpiece Combo.description:
Mark 2 Stress. The crew executes a rehearsed cinematic play: the driver crashes through a barrier, the runner kills the lights, the sniper pins someone down, the bruiser opens a path, or the face creates a distraction. Choose two:

  1. The crew immediately moves anywhere within Far range, ignoring difficult terrain, cover, crowds, or minor obstacles;
  2. One PC within Far range must succeed on an Agility or Instinct Reaction Roll or mark 2 Stress;
  3. The crew’s next attack gains advantage and deals +1d8 damage;
  4. A door, route, vehicle, piece of cover, or objective becomes compromised, exposed, blocked, or moved into danger.
Advantage and +1d8 damage on the next attack.

Cover Each Other.description: When this adversary would mark HP, mark a Stress to reduce the damage severity by one threshold.

Combat Eidolon Frame.description: A neural-linked war machine deployed when infantry, drones, and ordinary armor are no longer enough.
Combat Eidolon Frame.motivesAndTactics: Dominate space, complete the mission, reshape the battlefield

Mecha Structure.description:
This Eidolon adversary reduces damage it would take by half unless the effect comes from another Eidolon.

On the sheet: resistance to physical and techno damage. Against another Eidolon's attack, ignore the resistance.

Frame Pattern.description:
When this Eidolon enters the scene, choose one frame pattern:

  • Assault Frame: Its standard attacks deal +1d10 damage.
  • Guardian Frame: The Eidolon and any of its allies within Close range gain +1 Difficulty.

Battlefield Tactics.description:
Mark a Stress and choose one:

  • Suppress: Attack a target within Far range. On a success, it cannot voluntarily mark an Armor Slot, mark Stress, or spend Hope until it rolls with Hope.
  • Ram: Attack a target within Melee range. On a success, the target is pushed back to Close range, marks 1 Stress, and becomes temporarily Restrained.
  • Breach Path: Destroy, open, cross, or force through one obstacle within Far range.

Ram.description: Rammed by the Eidolon: pushed back to Close range and temporarily Restrained.

Suppress.description: Suppressed: cannot voluntarily mark an Armor Slot, mark Stress, or spend Hope until rolling with Hope.

Reactor Surge.description: When this Eidolon marks HP, mark a Stress to immediately choose one: move within Far range, clear a temporary condition, or give its next attack advantage.

Data Cult Oracle.description: A human body carrying too many machine voices and one prophecy.

Unwanted Revelation.description: When a PC rolls with Fear within Close range, they must answer one question the Oracle asks about their fear, desire, or cyberware and then mark a Stress.

Convert the Weak.description: Mark a Stress. A target within Far range must make a Presence Reaction Roll. On a failure, they mark 2 Stress and become temporarily Vulnerable.

Cult Transmission.description: Mark 2 Stress. Until this adversary’s next Spotlight, the Oracle’s allies within Close range gain +1 Difficulty and their attacks deal +1d6 techno damage.
Until the Data Cult Oracle's next Spotlight: +1 Difficulty and +1d6 techno damage.

Signal Martyr.description: When this adversary is defeated, one Digital Ghost within Far range clears 2 Stress and 1 HP.

Digital Wraith.description: A predatory AI ghost wearing the shape of something the victim almost remembers.

Unstable Render.description: The Digital Wraith does not occupy space like a physical creature. It appears through AR static, camera feeds, and corrupted sensors. When a PC attacks the Digital Wraith, they must choose one: mark 1 Stress to lock onto the correct signal, or make the attack with disadvantage. A PC who has created a Breach against the local network this scene ignores this effect.

Possess Device.description: Mark a Stress to possess a vehicle, device, weapon, or implant within Far range. This adversary may immediately activate, move, or attack from it.

Fear Echo.description: When a PC rolls with Fear within Far range, they see something personal in the signal and mark 1 Stress.

Digital Vanish.description: When this adversary marks HP, it becomes Hidden and reappears through another connected device within Far range.

Tyfar Kill Platform.description: A walking weapons platform with enough firepower to turn cover into a grave.

Walking Arsenal.description: When this adversary deals Major damage, the target’s cover is destroyed. When this adversary succeeds against a target without cover, add +1d10 to the damage roll.

Stabilizer Lock.description: This adversary cannot be pushed, Restrained, or moved against its will unless it has marked half or more of its HP.

Spin Up.description: Mark a Stress and make a standard attack roll. It targets all creatures within Very Close range of the original target.

Armor-Piercing Burst.description: When this adversary’s attack succeeds against a PC, that PC must mark an Armor Slot without receiving its benefits. If the PC cannot mark an Armor Slot, they mark a Stress instead.

Cyber Hunter.description: A remote-controlled ace pilot and augmented sniper operating three contracts ahead of everyone else.

Target Package.description: When this adversary damages a PC, that PC becomes Marked until the end of the scene or until they break line of sight for a full Spotlight.

Marked (Cyber Hunter).description: Marked by the Cyber Hunter until the end of the scene or until breaking line of sight for a full Spotlight: their attacks against this target have advantage and ignore cover.

Piercing Shot.description: Attacks against Marked targets have advantage and ignore cover.

Remote Reposition.description: Mark a Stress to move anywhere within Far range and make a standard attack against a Marked target.

Blackout Shot.description: Mark 2 Stress and attack a Marked target. On a success, deal damage and disable the target’s cyberware until it marks a Stress to re-enable it.
Cyberware disabled until marking 1 Stress to re-enable it.

Hold The Breath.description: When this adversary fails an attack roll, mark a Stress to reroll the d20.

Ares-Tyrant Eidolon.description: A Deus-Class assault Eidolon built around a war intelligence that does not accept retreat.

Mecha Structure.description:
This Eidolon adversary reduces damage it would take by half unless the effect comes from another Eidolon.

On the sheet: resistance to physical and techno damage. Against another Eidolon's attack, ignore the resistance.

Ares Overdrive.description: When this adversary deals Major damage, the target also marks 1 Stress.

Thermal Talon.description: Mark a Stress to attack a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 4d12+10 techno damage. The target is also Overheated and takes an extra 2d6 techno damage if they are still Overheated at the end of their action.

Overheated.description: Overheated: takes an extra 2d6 techno damage if still Overheated at the end of their own action.

War God Awakens.description: Mark 3 Stress. Until the end of the scene, all its attacks gain advantage and +1d12, but any PC who deals damage to it gains 1 Hope.
Until the end of the scene: all attacks with advantage and +1d12 damage. Any PC who deals damage to it gains 1 Hope.

No Retreat.description: When a PC moves away from this adversary, mark a Stress to move within Close range of them and make a standard attack as a reaction.

Hades Shard.description: A broken fragment of the Deus-Class AI that killed the old internet.
Hades Shard.motivesAndTactics: Consume systems, erase identity, birth ghosts

Digital Body.description:
This adversary is immune to physical damage unless it is dealt to the device where it is hosted.

On the sheet: immunity to physical damage. When attacking the device that hosts it, ignore the immunity.

Digital Afterlife.description: When a creature within Far range marks its last Hit Point, Hades creates a Digital Ghost echo of them.

Identity Collapse.description: Mark 2 Stress. One target within Far range must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, they mark 2 Stress and cannot use Experiences until their next rest.
Cannot use Experiences until the next rest.

Ghost Birth.description: Mark 3 Stress and choose one connected device or cyberware implant within Far range. A Digital Ghost manifestation emerges from it as a temporary threat.

Dead Network.description: When a PC creates a Breach within Far range, Hades may mark a Stress to corrupt it. The PC marks 1 Stress.

Board Executive.description: A corporate sovereign with lawyers, kill-teams, hostage clauses, and legal ownership of the battlefield.

Liability Shield.description: While at least one corporate ally is within Close range, this adversary gains +2 Difficulty.
+2 Difficulty. Turn it on while at least one corporate ally is within Close range.

Hostile Acquisition.description: Mark 2 Stress. One target within Far range must make a Presence Reaction Roll. On a failure, they cannot gain Hope until the end of the scene.
Cannot gain Hope until the end of the scene.

Asset Freeze.description: Mark a Stress and choose one PC. Until the end of the scene, they must mark 1 Stress before using credits, contacts, gear access, a vehicle, or a connected system.
Until the end of the scene, must mark 1 Stress before using credits, contacts, gear access, a vehicle, or a connected system.

Contractual Violence.description: When a PC threatens this adversary, mark a Stress to summon two corporate allies of Tier 2 or lower that enter the scene within Close range of it.

Plausible Deniability.description: When this adversary would mark HP, redirect the consequence to one corporate ally, bodyguard, hostage, legal shield, decoy, or escape protocol within Close range.

Chrome Reaper.description: A legendary full-body cyborg, known to some as the Boogeyman of the New Dark Age, who remembers being human as a weakness.

Cyberpsycho.description: When this adversary deals damage, the GM gains a Fear.

Weapon Switch.description: Make a standard attack. On a roll of 15+, choose one: push the target to Close range, make them mark 1 Stress, or deal +1d10 damage.

Personal Threat.description:
Mark 2 Stress and choose one PC within Far range. Until that PC rolls with Hope, attacks against them gain advantage and deal +1d10 damage.

On the sheet: the effect uses the Vulnerable condition (attacks against them with advantage); add the +1d10 damage by hand.
The Chrome Reaper's personal threat: until rolling with Hope, attacks against this character gain advantage and deal +1d10 damage.

Unfair Reflexes.description: When a PC rolls with Hope against this adversary, mark a Stress to change it to a roll with Fear and then immediately move within Close range or make a standard attack.

Chrome Supremacy.description: When a PC causes this adversary to mark HP, become Vulnerable, become Restrained, or lose sight of a PC, this adversary may mark a Stress to negate this effect and make that PC mark a Stress instead.

Black Hand.description: Black Hand is not the best shot in the world, the fastest blade, or the strongest chrome body. He is worse: he is good enough at everything to kill specialists at their own game.

A Legend Like You.description: The first time each scene a PC spends Hope while within Far range of Black Hand, he may immediately make a standard attack against them.

Contract Target.description: When this adversary damages a PC, that PC becomes his Target until the end of the scene or until another PC deals Major damage to Black Hand. Black Hand’s attacks against marked targets deal +1d8 damage.

Alvo (Black Hand).name: Target (Black Hand)
Alvo (Black Hand).description: Black Hand's Target until the end of the scene or until another character deals Major damage to him: Black Hand's attacks against this target deal +1d8 damage.

Black Hand Guns.description:
Make a standard attack, then choose a weapon:

  • Hand Cannon: The target marks a Stress.
  • Mono-Blade: If the target is within Melee range, they mark two Armor Slots without receiving their benefits.
  • Smart Rifle: The next attack against the target gains +2.
  • Shock Gauntlet: The target becomes temporarily Vulnerable on Major damage.

Smart Rifle.description: The next attack against this target gains +2.

Hard Entry.description: When a PC rolls with Hope against this adversary, mark a Stress to immediately move within Close range, draw a new weapon, and either clear a temporary condition or gain advantage on the next attack.

Eidolon Drop.description: When the GM spends 3 Fear after Black Hand has marked at least 5 HP, he deploys his Eidolon. Clear all temporary conditions from Black Hand and replace his stat block with @UUID[Compendium.edgeheart-cyberpunk.edgeheart-adversaries.Actor.j0oIESpcobql1C5J]{The Raven Eidolon}, keeping his marked Stress and features. Any PCs who were marked as his Target remain marked.

The Raven Eidolon.description: Black Hand's Eidolon, deployed with Eidolon Drop when the contract gets too heavy. It keeps Black Hand's marked Stress and features.

Merciless Advance.description: Mark a Stress, move within Far range, and make a standard attack. If the PC is marked as a Target, this attack has advantage.

Killbox Execution.description: Mark 3 Stress. The Raven floods the area within Far range of it with missiles, suppressive fire, and close-range assault force. Make a standard attack against all PCs inside the area. On a success, deal damage and the PC becomes marked as Black Hand’s Target.

Alvo (Black Hand).name: Target (Black Hand)
Alvo (Black Hand).description: Black Hand's Target until the end of the scene or until another character deals Major damage to him: Black Hand's attacks against this target deal +1d8 damage.

Black Hand Override.description: When this adversary would fail an attack roll, mark 2 Stress to reroll the d20. If the reroll succeeds, the target also becomes temporarily Vulnerable.

Neon Night Market.description: A crowded market of food stalls, chrome dealers, counterfeit fashion, gang scouts, and illegal tech.

Crowded Flow.description:
PCs have advantage on rolls to hide in the crowd, but disadvantage on rolls to notice threats beyond Close range.

Who is watching from the crowd?

Black-Market Offer.description:
Present a useful item, cyberware lead, or contact at a cost.

What does the seller really want?

Wrong Eyes.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear on a social or stealth roll, a gang scout recognizes them or mistakes them for someone else.

Whose reputation did they inherit?

Low-Sec Data Office.description: A cheap corporate office full of badge locks, glass walls, tired staff, and too many cameras.

Badge Logic.description:
PCs can make an Interface Roll to create a Breach against doors, cameras, or elevators. On a roll with Fear, security starts asking questions.

Whose badge still works here?

Camera Sweep.description:
Choose a PC in an exposed area. They must mark a Stress or become recorded and traceable.

Who reviews the footage?

Reception Alarm.description:
When a PC fails a social roll, summon a Sitil Security Guard within Far range.

What did the receptionist notice?

Megablock Stairwell.description: A vertical maze of emergency stairs, leaking pipes, locked floors, and neighbors who know when to shut their doors.

Bad Angles.description:
Ranged attacks beyond Very Close range have disadvantage unless the attacker controls a higher position.

Who has the high ground?

Door Slams Open.description:
Introduce civilians, gang lookouts, security, or a new route through an apartment.

Who lives behind this door?

Down the Stairs.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear while moving, they slip, crash, or get blocked. They mark a Stress or move down one range band.

What broke under their feet?

Street-Level Stakeout.description: A quiet surveillance job where everyone is waiting for the first mistake.

Eyes Everywhere.description:
PCs may make Instinct or Knowledge Rolls to identify watchers. On a success, gain advantage on the next stealth or counter-surveillance roll.

Who is watching the watchers?

The Target Moves.description:
Move the objective to a new location within Far range.

Why did they leave early?

Burned Position.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, reveal that their hiding place, signal, or cover identity is compromised.

Who burned them?

Highway Kill Run.description:
A high-speed chase through broken roads, traffic drones, abandoned checkpoints, and ambush vehicles.

Also works with: Cordon Eidolon.

The Chase.description:
When this Traversal starts, place a Chase Die (d8) on this card with the 4 value facing up. When a PC makes an action related to the chase, turn the die according to the result:

  • Success with Hope: increase the die by 2.
  • Success with Fear: increase the die by 1.
  • Failure with Hope: decrease the die by 1.
  • Failure with Fear: decrease the die by 2.

If the die reaches 8, the PCs succeed in the Highway Kill Run, either by escaping or by reaching the target. If the die reaches 0, the PCs fail, either getting captured or letting the target escape.

Why are we chasing them, anyway?

Vehicle Momentum.description:
When a PC succeeds on a vehicle roll with Hope, they may move one additional range or create an opening for an ally.

Who knows this road best?

Road Hazard.description:
Drop traffic, wreckage, drones, civilians, or a collapsing overpass into the route. Drivers must make an Agility Reaction Roll or the vehicle becomes Damaged.

What did the road hide?

Pursuit Escalation.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear while driving, a new hostile vehicle enters at Far range.

Who joined the chase?

Corporate Heist Floor.description: A secure corporate level built around vaults, hostages, panic rooms, and silent alarms.

Objective Clock.description:
The crew must complete a Progress Countdown (4) to seize the item, extract the target, or crack the vault. Each roll with Fear advances security response.

What part of the plan was wrong?

Lockdown Doors.description:
Seal a room, hallway, elevator, or vault. Creatures inside must mark a Stress or become temporarily Restrained.

Who triggered the lockdown?

Hostage Pressure.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, place a civilian, employee, VIP, or target in immediate danger.

Who becomes leverage?

Haunted Subway Node.description: An abandoned transit station where screens whisper names and trains arrive from routes that no longer exist.

Signal Haunting.description:
Connected devices show false exits, dead passengers, impossible reflections, or messages from familiar voices. PCs relying on sensors have disadvantage unless they first create a Breach.

Whose voice comes through the speakers?

Ghost Train.description:
A phantom train screams through the station. All creatures in a line must make an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d8+4 techno damage and become temporarily Vulnerable.

Where is the train going?
Hit by the ghost train: temporarily Vulnerable.

False Exit.description:
Choose one visible exit, tunnel, or door. It appears safe, open, or closer than it truly is. The first PC who moves toward it must mark 1 Stress and succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or mark 1 Hit Point and end their movement somewhere dangerous, exposed, or separated.

Where did the station want them to go?

Possessed Platform.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, the environment moves them within Close range or separates them from one ally.

What platform did they step onto?

Black Clinic Under Siege.description: A hidden clinic filled with half-finished surgeries, illegal medicine, and people too valuable to lose.

Fragile Patients.description:
Any attack that rolls with Fear risks harming a patient, damaging medical gear, or contaminating the operating room.

Who is on the table?

Emergency Procedure.description:
A PC can attempt a Knowledge or Finesse Roll to stabilize a patient or device. On a success, one ally clears 1 Stress.

What illegal procedure is halfway complete?

Power Failure.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, lights fail, life support flickers, or doors unlock. All medical actions have disadvantage until someone restores power.

Who wanted the power cut?

Blacksite Extraction.description:
A hidden corporate facility where the objective is alive, unstable, and probably not human anymore.

Also works with: Cordon Eidolon.

Containment Protocol.description:
The objective cannot leave until the crew completes a Progress Countdown (6) to disable locks, restraints, sedation, or legal failsafes.

What was the objective built to contain?

Sterile Kill Team.description:
Deploy a corporate squad within Far range or activate a turret, drone, or sealed corridor.

Who gave the kill order?

Erase Evidence.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, a server, witness, body, or clue begins self-deleting.

What truth is about to disappear?

Gang War Block.description: A city block locked in open gang warfare, burning cars, rooftop shooters, and civilians trapped between colors.

Crossfire.description:
When a creature moves through open ground, they must mark a Stress or make an Agility Roll to avoid stray fire.

Who is shooting from above?

Claim the Block.description:
A gang force seizes a street, rooftop, store, or vehicle. It becomes dangerous terrain until cleared.

Whose symbol is painted there?

Reputation Test.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear on a social or combat roll, someone challenges their name, crew, or loyalty.

Who wants to embarrass them?

Eidolon Deployment Zone.description:
A shattered battlefield designed for machines too large for streets and too dangerous for buildings.

Also works with: Cordon Eidolon.
Eidolon Deployment Zone.impulses: Shake ground, expose cover, invite escalation

Eidolon Scale.description:
Ordinary cover, vehicles, walls, and drones are destroyed after taking Major or Severe damage from an Eidolon-scale attack.

What used to stand here?

Heavy Debris.description:
Collapse a crane, wall, tower, vehicle, or bridge. Creatures within Close range must make an Agility Reaction Roll or take 3d8+6 impact damage.

What falls first?

Sensor Bloom.description:
When a PC deploys an Eidolon or rolls with Fear, all factions nearby learn something large is active.

Who answers the signal?

Digital Ghost Cathedral.description: A ruined data center where corrupted AI speak through prayer loops, broken ads, and dead family photos.

Litany of Static.description:
At the start of a scene, each PC with connected cyberware must mark a Stress and hear a voice asking them a personal question.

What does the Ghost know?

Icon Becomes Monster.description:
Choose a screen, statue, drone, vehicle, or body. It animates as a temporary Digital Ghost threat until destroyed or disconnected.

What image does it wear?

Mirrored Dead.description:
Spend up to 3 Fear and choose the same number of PCs in the scene. The Cathedral generates a corrupted echo of them through screens, speakers, drones, old photos, security footage, or AR static. Until the end of the scene or until the PC rolls with Hope, when that PC would make an action roll, the GM reveals a distorted memory, fear, regret, or false version of their past. They must choose one:

  • Mark 1 Stress and become temporarily Vulnerable.
  • Give disadvantage to the roll as the echo interferes with their senses.
  • Mark 2 Armor Slots as the echo "attacks" them.

What part of them did the Cathedral learn to imitate?

Prayer Loop.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, marked Stress cannot be cleared until the PC leaves the Haunted Zone or severs the signal.

What phrase keeps repeating?

Dead Pantheon Breach.description:
A place where the Blackwall thins and Theoi-derived systems start dreaming in public.

Also works with: Blackwall Seraph.

Reality Through Machines.description:
Cameras, implants, drones, vehicles, and screens may show different versions of the same scene. PCs must succeed on an Instinct or Knowledge Roll before trusting digital information.

Which version is lying?

Ghost Incursion.description:
Spawn a Digital Ghost or possess a connected machine within Far range.

What came through the breach?

Root-Level Intrusion.description:
Choose a connected device within Far range. It receives a command from beyond the Blackwall and turns against its user or the environment around it. A PC directly affected must make an Interface Reaction Roll. On a failure, they mark 3 Stress and the device misfires, locks, crashes, exposes them, moves them into danger, or attacks a nearby target. On a success, they mark 1 Stress and force the system back under control.

What machine obeyed a dead god?

The God Notices.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, they must mark a Stress or lose 1 Hope as the signal speaks directly to them.

What name does it call them?

Corporate Tower Coup.description: A boardroom, gala, hostage floor, and command bunker all pretending to be the same building.

Legal Battlefield.description:
Successful social rolls can disable security, redirect guards, freeze accounts, or change objectives. Failed social rolls with Fear create legal, financial, or hostage complications.

Who owns the room?

Hostile Vote.description:
A faction inside the tower changes sides, reveals leverage, or calls armed support.

Who bought their loyalty?

Executive Evacuation.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, the true target begins escaping through a private route.

Which exit was never on the map?

Blackwall Storm Highway.description:
A ruined highway where vehicles race through lightning, broken infrastructure, and corrupted machine weather.

Also works with: Handler’s Hound, Blackwall Seraph.

Machine Weather.description:
Vehicles and connected gear glitch under the storm. On any vehicle roll with Fear, the vehicle becomes Damaged unless the driver marks a Stress.

What system flickers first?

Black Lightning.description:
Strike a vehicle, drone, Eidolon, or connected device within Far range. It must make a Reaction Roll or take 4d8+6 techno damage.

What does the lightning spell out?

Route Collapse.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, destroy one route, bridge, tunnel, ramp, or exit.

Who knew the road would fail?

Elite Contract Auction.description: A secret auction where corps, gangs, digital cults, and mercenary legends bid on a person, weapon, AI shard, or Eidolon key.

Everyone Wants It.description:
Every faction present has a different objective. When PCs create an opening, another faction may exploit it.

Who is bidding with blood instead of credits?

Raise the Price.description:
Reveal a new cost: hostage, debt, public exposure, cyberware key, blackmail, or a rival bid.

What is the real price?

Masks Off.description:
When a PC rolls with Fear, reveal a hidden identity, disguised enemy, double agent, or secret buyer.

Who was never supposed to be here?

Edgeheart Loot.description: Roll by rarity: Common 1d10, Uncommon 1d10 or 2d10, Rare 2d10 or 3d10, Legendary 3d10 or 4d10 (change the table formula, or roll and choose the result).

Edgeheart Consumables.description: Roll by rarity: Common 1d10, Uncommon 1d10 or 2d10, Rare 2d10 or 3d10, Legendary 3d10 or 4d10 (change the table formula, or roll and choose the result).
